headline: Government says its 'Your First Home' equity loan scheme will be confirmed in the October Budget
detail: On 26 September the government said the new homebuying equity loan scheme would be confirmed in next month's Budget, according to Reuters. The FT reported that the scheme revives Help to Buy, with the stated aim of boosting housebuilding.

headline: US President Trump rejects Iran's proposal for a week-long ceasefire to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
detail: The FT reported on 26 September that Tehran had offered a one-week pause in hostilities to start peace talks on the seven-month conflict. Reuters later reported that Iran still wants a diplomatic solution and that mediators had not formally passed on a US rejection.

headline: PM Burnham says social care reform will be funded by new taxes and put to voters at the next general election
detail: On 27 September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said his plan for a national care service would be free at the point of use, with the cost shared across the population through new taxes. He said the reform would be hard to deliver in the current parliament, and the next election may not come until 2029.

headline: Chancellor Healey says UK capital gains tax is the lowest of any major European economy, ahead of the October Budget
detail: Chancellor John Healey made the comment on Sunday 27 September while discussing business confidence and competitiveness on capital taxes, City AM reported. The report said the remarks raise the prospect of another capital gains tax increase at the Budget.

headline: Chancellor Healey to set out a £6bn Royal Navy plan in his Labour conference speech
detail: The FT reported that the Chancellor will pledge that British firms will build three new floating docks on the Clyde as part of a £6bn Royal Navy plan. The speech is due on Tuesday.

headline: UK Business Secretary calls a possible US diesel export ban a significant concern; UK gets about a sixth of its diesel from the US
detail: US President Trump said he is seriously considering a diesel export ban, with a 90-day ban or more limited voluntary restrictions reported to be under consideration. UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said a full ban would be a significant concern for Britain but noted that UK fuel supply is diverse.

headline: Oil rises more than 1% after Trump rejects Iran proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
detail: A wire reported that oil prices climbed more than 1% after US President Trump rejected Iran's peace proposal. US stock futures were reported slightly lower.

headline: FT reports the Bank of England's balance sheet has grown over the past year despite quantitative tightening
detail: The Financial Times reported on 28 September that the Bank of England's balance sheet has stopped shrinking and is larger than it was a year ago. The report gave no figures.

headline: Brent trades above $106 a barrel as 10-year US Treasury yields reach 5.2%, adding pressure on government bonds
detail: The Financial Times reported early on 28 September that Brent was above $106 a barrel and 10-year Treasury yields had reached 5.2%. Wire headlines also reported higher Japanese government bond yields, citing concerns over the Iran conflict and inflation.

headline: BoE MPC member Dhingra flags concern that elevated interest rates could weigh on investment and reduce supply capacity
detail: Bank of England external MPC member Swati Dhingra said she is concerned that high rates could damage business investment and cut the economy's supply capacity, according to a newswire headline on 28 September. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: ONS publishes revised Labour Force Survey series adjusted with PAYE data, showing a larger recent fall in employment
detail: The ONS has reworked its Labour Force Survey data using HMRC PAYE figures to correct for the drop in survey responses since the pandemic. The revised series shows a deeper fall in employment early in the pandemic, a stronger recovery afterwards and a bigger decline in recent months.

headline: Defence Secretary Streeting signals further defence spending announcements in the October Budget
detail: UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said more on defence spending will come at the Budget. He gave no figures.

headline: BoE's Ramsden says inflation risks have tilted to the upside and a Bank Rate rise could be warranted if pressures keep building
detail: BoE Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said the current policy stance remains restrictive, and named energy prices, food prices and wage settlements as his main focus. He said he does not expect further QE to be considered soon, and described the QT plan and its September changes as credible and well received by markets.

headline: BoE's Ramsden says Bank's gilt sales will start with the longest maturities, reported as 2033 to 2049
detail: Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said the Bank of England's gilt sales will begin at the long end of the maturity range. One report gave the range as 2033 to 2049 and another as 2035 to 2049. In the same remarks he said he wanted QT pushed further into the background and that a period of higher, longer-lasting headline inflation is shaping his thinking.

headline: US crude futures rise more than 4% to a session high of $96.44 a barrel as US-Iran peace efforts stall
detail: US crude futures rose more than 4% to a session high of $96.44 a barrel after peace talks between the US and Iran stalled.

headline: Global bond sell-off deepens as Brent rises above $108 and 10-year US Treasury yield tops 5.2%
detail: The FT reports that Brent crude has climbed above $108 a barrel and the 10-year US Treasury yield has passed 5.2% as hopes of a US-Iran deal fade.

headline: Chancellor Healey pledges to meet the fiscal rules and says fiscal discipline will be at the core of his Budget
detail: In his Labour conference speech, Chancellor Healey said the government will stick to its fiscal rules and keep control of the public finances. He called current debt levels an affront to the party's values and said the government must act to cut the welfare bill.

headline: UK diesel prices hit a record 199.18p per litre, according to RAC data
detail: City AM reported on 28 September that RAC figures showed diesel reaching a record 199.18p per litre. The report said UK borrowing costs were also rising ahead of the Budget.

headline: Chancellor Healey tells Labour conference there is no spare money for extra public service spending
detail: In his Labour conference speech on 28 September, the Chancellor said the public finances have less room than in the Blair years because growth is lower and debt is higher. The FT reported that the speech was preparing the party for possible tax rises in the Budget.

headline: US and Iran to hold separate talks with Qatari mediators, with no US officials at Iran's New York meeting
detail: An official told Reuters that Qatari mediators are expected to meet Iranian Foreign Minister Araqchi in New York and the US side separately on Monday or Tuesday. Iran's ISNA reported that no US representatives will attend Araqchi's meeting.

headline: Citi/YouGov: UK public year-ahead inflation expectations rise to 4.5% in September, long-term measure up to 4.3%
detail: The Citi/YouGov survey puts UK year-ahead public inflation expectations at 4.5% in September, compared with 3.9% previously. The longer-term measure rose to 4.3% from 4.1% in August.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says the inflation outlook for 2027 and 2028 is higher than expected and backs a measured policy response
detail: In a speech to the European Parliament, ECB President Lagarde said the inflation shock is too large to look through and that a measured response is appropriate. She said she sees no sign yet that inflation is becoming embedded, and that risks remain to the upside for inflation and to the downside for growth.

headline: ECB's Lagarde puts rates at the upper end of the neutral range as traders cut October hike odds below 40%
detail: ECB President Lagarde said euro area rates are at the upper end of the neutral range but that policy is not being set by reference to the neutral rate. Market pricing reported on 28 September showed less than a 40% chance of an ECB rate rise in October.

headline: PM Burnham says the defence investment plan will be fully funded at the Budget; social care funding details due tomorrow
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said in an LBC Radio interview on 28 September that the defence investment plan will be fully funded at the Budget. He also said details of social care funding will be published the following day.

headline: UK 10-year gilt yield rises to 5.441%, its highest level since July 2007
detail: A market newswire reported on 28 September that the 10-year gilt yield had climbed to 5.441%, the highest since July 2007. The move came as the global bond sell-off continued.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs 10bp to 5.27%; 2-year hits 4.952%, highest since May 2024
detail: Market newswires reported on 28 September that the US 10-year Treasury yield had risen by 10bp to 5.27%. The 2-year yield reached 4.952%, its highest since May 2024.

headline: US official says Trump is prepared to ease Iran sanctions and release frozen assets in return for nuclear progress
detail: A US official told Al Jazeera on 28 September that indirect talks with Iran through intermediaries are positive, but no deal is possible unless the nuclear issue is addressed. None of the posts reported a market reaction.

headline: Al Hadath reports Iran agrees to suspend uranium enrichment for US sanctions relief; US source puts deal chances as extremely slim
detail: Al Hadath, citing sources, reported that Iran has agreed to halt uranium enrichment in exchange for easing of US sanctions. Shortly afterwards, a US source involved in the negotiations told Al Arabiya that the gaps remain wide and the chances of an agreement are extremely slim, and Iranian officials were separately reported to be pessimistic about a deal before the US midterms.

headline: Saudi Arabia resumes oil exports via East-West pipeline at about 3.5m bpd as US crude gives up gains near $92
detail: Sources said Saudi Arabia has resumed oil exports through the East-West pipeline after repairs, with Aramco running it at a throughput of around 3.5 million barrels a day. US crude was reported to have reversed its earlier gains and to be trading near $92 a barrel.

headline: Fed's Cook sees broadening US inflation pressure from AI and the Middle East conflict, and warns rate cuts could fuel inflation
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said in a speech on 28 September that she sees signs of broadening pressure in inflation data and expects continued inflation pressure in the coming months from AI-driven demand and the Middle East conflict. She said lowering rates to offset any AI-related rise in unemployment could fuel inflation, and that future rate adjustments will depend on inflation and labour market data.

headline: Brent crude settles up 96 cents at $105.28 a barrel; WTI closes at $92.60
detail: Brent futures ended 28 September 0.92% higher at $105.28 a barrel, while NYMEX WTI November futures settled 19 cents higher at $92.60. NYMEX diesel settled at $4.7553 a gallon and natural gas at $3.00/MMBtu.

headline: Trump again threatens to ban US diesel exports to bring down domestic prices
detail: Semafor reported on 28 September that the US president repeated his threat to halt diesel exports from the US, the world's largest diesel producer and exporter. Separately, he said the US would win the Iran war very soon and that fuel prices would then fall sharply.

headline: Italian and French 10y10y forward yields rise about 10bp in a single session as the long end sells off
detail: A market economist reported on 28 September that 10-year-10-year forward yields for both Italy and France had risen by around 10bp during the day. No gilt market reaction was given.

headline: Iranian official denies reports that Iran has softened its nuclear stance and says no nuclear talks are under way
detail: Fars News reported an Iranian official as saying Iran's nuclear position is unchanged and that reports of flexibility are wrong. Separately, Al Jazeera reported that a new Iranian proposal puts off nuclear commitments until a first phase is implemented, and a senior Iranian security committee official said the Strait of Hormuz, not the nuclear issue, is now the focus of negotiations.

headline: Iran's parliament considers a bill to leave the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, Fars reports
detail: Fars News cited an Iranian lawmaker as saying parliament is weighing a bill for Iran to exit the NPT. No timing for a vote was given.

headline: Iran's foreign minister says Qatari mediators will take Tehran's proposals to the US and hopes for a final US reply by Tuesday
detail: Iranian state news agency IRNA reported that Foreign Minister Araqchi said the Strait of Hormuz will reopen only if the supreme leader's conditions are met. Separately, President Trump said he had not given Iran any sanctions relief.

headline: Trump denies offering Iran sanctions relief or frozen funds and calls the Axios report untrue
detail: On Truth Social, President Trump said he had offered Iran nothing and demanded that Axios withdraw its report that he had offered sanctions relief and the release of frozen funds. His denial came as the US 10-year Treasury yield stood at levels last seen in 2007, with the sell-off attributed to faltering US-Iran diplomacy and concerns about oil prices.

headline: UK mortgage approvals fall to 54,918 against 56,100 expected; mortgage lending £4.41bn
detail: Bank of England data showed mortgage approvals below the 56,053 previous reading and the 56,100 forecast. Net mortgage lending was £4.410bn against £4.4bn expected (previous revised to £4.082bn), and M4 money supply rose 0.4% after -0.3%.

headline: ECB's Kazimir says rate hike was unavoidable and January repricing will be key, with energy prices still a major factor
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazimir also stressed the need for flexibility and said there is plenty of time.

headline: EU energy commissioner tells US counterpart that restricting energy flows helps no one; Irish minister calls diesel ban unlikely
detail: The EU energy commissioner said the message was sent to the US following threats of a US diesel export ban. Ireland's energy minister said such a ban would significantly affect the EU but did not appear likely to happen.

headline: IEA's Birol says Europe gets 50% of its diesel from the US and further strategic reserve releases would be discussed if needed
detail: The International Energy Agency's executive director said Europe is among the regions most exposed in the diesel market and that the agency is in talks with countries about the situation.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker warns no regional state will sell oil if Iran cannot, and says regional infrastructure would not be safe
detail: Parliament speaker Qalibaf made the remarks according to Iranian state media. Separately, an IRGC spokesperson said the US has no option but to admit failure and leave the region.

headline: Spanish September flash CPI rises to 4.9% y/y against 4.6% expected; HICP at 5.0%
detail: Spain's flash CPI rose to 4.9% y/y in September from 4.3% (forecast 4.6%), and 0.3% m/m against 0.1% expected. HICP was 5.0% y/y (forecast 4.9%, previous 4.6%) and core CPI 3.1% y/y (forecast 3.0%, previous 2.9%).

headline: Brent crude futures rise more than 2% to $107.44 a barrel; December contract at $99.87
detail: Brent front-month futures gained over 2% in Asian trading to $107.44 a barrel, with the December contract also up more than 2% at $99.87.

headline: RBA raises cash rate 25bp to 4.60% as expected and says further tightening may be needed as Middle East conflict lifts energy prices
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate target from 4.35% to 4.60%, its third hike this year, in line with forecasts. It said inflation remains elevated, upside risks have emerged and energy prices far exceed its August forecast, and that it will raise rates further if needed. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7026 after the decision.

headline: US-Iran war adds €100bn to EU fuel bill, FT reports as bloc's energy ministers meet in Dublin
detail: The Financial Times reports a warning that the US-Iran conflict has added €100bn to the EU's fuel bill. EU energy ministers are meeting in Dublin.

headline: EU declares full solidarity with Estonia over attack blamed on Russia; Lavrov says Europe is waging war on Russia
detail: An EU spokesman said the bloc stands in full solidarity with Estonia after an attack attributed to Russia. At a press conference, Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov responded to Western claims of Russian hybrid warfare by saying Europe is waging war against Russia.

headline: Italy's energy minister to ask US Energy Secretary about a possible US diesel export ban on Tuesday
detail: Italy's energy minister said he would speak with US Energy Secretary Wright later on Tuesday and raise a possible US ban on diesel exports.

headline: UKMTO receives late report of vessel struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz on 28 September
detail: UK Maritime Trade Operations received a late report that a vessel was hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 28 September.

headline: Iranian army offers 10bn toman reward for capture of any American soldier
detail: An Iranian army spokesperson announced a reward of 10bn toman to any Iranian who captures an American soldier, dead or alive. Separately, Qatar's foreign ministry said it is still passing messages between the US and Iran.

headline: UK sells £4.25bn of 10-year gilts at 5.383% average yield, highest for newly issued 10-year debt since 1999
detail: The morning 10-year gilt auction raised £4.25bn at an average yield of 5.383%, a reporter noted. That is the highest yield on new 10-year issuance since 1999. Secondary market yields were higher in 2007, but no 10-year gilts were issued that year.

headline: BRC survey shows shop price and food inflation easing in September while pipeline cost pressures build
detail: The British Retail Consortium's September shop price survey showed overall shop price inflation and food inflation both easing. The BRC said retailers still face rising cost pressures. The post gave no figures.

headline: UK consumer credit rises £2.464bn, above £1.9bn forecast and £2.006bn previously
detail: Bank of England figures put net consumer credit at £2.464bn, against a forecast of £1.9bn and £2.006bn in the previous month.

headline: North Sea Forties crude loadings are set at eight cargoes for November
detail: This is the published November loading programme for the Forties crude grade.

headline: US to allow Iraqi Airways to fly Iranian pilgrims to and from Najaf as US-Iran peace talks resume
detail: Iraqi officials say the US will let Iranian travellers fly to and from Najaf. Separately, Reuters reports that major Gulf stock markets were mixed as investors weighed renewed diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran conflict.

headline: IEA's Birol warns Europe faces a very difficult winter and says another oil stock release is not a priority
detail: The IEA executive director said he hopes Europe and its allies will cooperate to limit energy risks. He said a further release of oil stocks is not at the top of the agenda.

headline: Trump backs Russia sanctions relief tied to a prisoner release, The Atlantic reports
detail: The Atlantic reports that President Trump expressed support for the plan a few months ago. It says the initiative is still at an early stage.

headline: EU energy commissioner rules out an EU-wide windfall tax and says any such levy should be set nationally
detail: The commissioner also said that, given current market conditions, taxes on electricity should be lower than taxes on gas.

headline: ECB's Escriva says policy is not yet restrictive and flags concern over the global rise in long-term rates
detail: Governing Council member Escriva said the ECB is not in restrictive territory, that the global upward path of long-term rates could add pressure on interest rates and that high energy prices could become anchored in inflation. He said he sees no second-round effects so far and that Spain is not considering moving its gold reserves.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev holds talks with US Treasury and Energy officials on ending the Ukraine war and on energy cooperation
detail: A US official described Monday's meeting in Washington as constructive and said the talks covered possible US-Russia energy initiatives once the war ends. Sources say Dmitriev met representatives of the US Treasury and Energy departments.

headline: Union leader warns PM Burnham against ending the pensions triple lock before his first conference speech
detail: The FT reports that a senior union leader said scrapping the triple lock would be electorally damaging. The warning came ahead of the Labour leader's first party conference speech as prime minister.

headline: Italy completes the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq
detail: A market newswire reported on 29 September that Italy has completed the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq.

headline: Wells Fargo Investment Institute lifts its end-2027 forecasts for the Fed funds rate and the 10-year Treasury yield
detail: The institute now forecasts the Fed policy rate at 4.75%-5.00% by the end of 2027, up from 4.00%-4.25%. Its forecast for the 10-year US Treasury yield rises to 5.25%-5.75%, from 4.50%-5.00%.

headline: Average UK diesel price reported to be close to £2 per litre, with the level expected within days
detail: A market newswire reported on 29 September that the average UK pump price of diesel is set to hit £2 a litre within days. The post gave no current price.

headline: Russian economy minister Reshetnikov is to attend a G20 meeting in the US, Interfax reports
detail: Interfax reported on 29 September that Russian Economy Minister Maxim Reshetnikov will take part in a G20 meeting being held in the United States.

headline: Netanyahu says there are signs Israel's enemies may try attacks ahead of elections and warns Israel can strike anywhere
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on 29 September that there are indications of possible attacks on Israel as its elections approach. He said Israel is able to strike its enemies at any place and time.

headline: Canadian GDP is flat in July, in line with forecasts, after 0.3% growth in June
detail: Statistics Canada's monthly GDP for July came in at 0.0% m/m, matching the 0.0% consensus. The previous month's reading was 0.3%.

headline: Oman's OQ considers buying two supertankers for floating storage and plans to more than double Duqm oil storage
detail: Oman state energy company OQ SAOC is reported to be evaluating buying two supertankers to lease out for floating storage at the port of Duqm. Oman also plans to more than double oil storage capacity at Duqm.

headline: US VP Vance says Washington believes Iran's Supreme Leader is alive and that Iran must behave for any deal
detail: US Vice President JD Vance made the remarks on 29 September, as US-Iran peace talks resume. He said Iran's conduct is a condition for any agreement.

headline: NATO's Rutte accuses Russia of a reckless campaign of hostile acts against allies and pledges more support for Ukraine
detail: The NATO secretary general spoke at a joint press conference with Lithuania's prime minister and said Russia is failing.

headline: Merz and five other EU leaders threaten to block the EU's next seven-year budget without large spending cuts
detail: The FT reports that the German chancellor and five other leaders want spending cuts running into hundreds of billions of euros as a condition of agreeing the budget.

headline: Zelenskiy says Russia attacked two foreign ships in the Odesa area
detail: Ukraine's president said Russian forces struck two foreign vessels near the Black Sea port of Odesa.

headline: South Korea says North Korean mines caused a DMZ blast that broke the armistice and calls for talks
detail: South Korea's defence minister said last week's blast injured two South Korean personnel, warranted a response and that Seoul will urge Pyongyang to hold talks to verify the facts.

headline: Rubio says a foreign state was involved in the incident near a UK airbase used by US forces to strike Iran
detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a foreign actor was involved in the incident, in which five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences, Reuters reported.

headline: Estonia blames Russian sabotage for an arson attack on a defence company
detail: An Estonian minister attributed the arson attack on the defence firm to Russia.

headline: EU energy ministers to meet in October on winter energy security; Irish minister says Europe's reserves are ample
detail: Ireland's energy minister said EU countries can make temporary tax changes to ease high energy costs and that ministers will discuss winter supply at an October meeting.

headline: IEA's Birol says member states may discuss further strategic oil reserve releases if needed
detail: On Tuesday the head of the International Energy Agency said member countries could consider releasing more strategic oil stocks onto the market in future, Reuters reports.

headline: BoE money and credit data show UK broad money growth holding at around 4%
detail: The Bank of England's money and credit release published this morning shows broad money growth staying subdued at roughly 4%.

headline: Kremlin says its decrees putting foreign firms' Russian units under temporary control will not change their ownership
detail: The Kremlin said the temporary administration decrees bring in external management and are partly a response to unfriendly countries' growing military involvement against Russia. It called the move reversible but said there are currently no grounds to reverse it. In the same briefing it denied involvement in the arson attack on an Estonian defence company and said it wants Iran to remain in the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

headline: Lufthansa says its extra jet fuel bill this year will exceed the €1.5bn flagged in August
detail: Lufthansa's chief executive said higher oil prices during the Iran war will push the airline's additional jet fuel costs above the €1.5bn estimate it gave in August, Reuters reports.

headline: Saudi Arabia resumes oil loadings at Red Sea port of Yanbu after East-West Pipeline restarts
detail: Trade sources and shipping data show that Saudi Arabia has restarted loadings at Yanbu after bringing the East-West Pipeline back into operation, Reuters reports.

headline: RBA raises cash rate by 25bp to 4.60%, its fourth increase this year
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board raised the cash rate target by 25bp to 4.60% at its meeting overnight. This is the fourth hike in 2026.

headline: PBOC cuts PSL rates by 25bp to 1.5% for 1-year and raises relending quotas by a combined 700bn yuan
detail: The People's Bank of China lowered pledged supplementary lending rates by 0.25 percentage points, taking the 1-year PSL rate to 1.5%, and changed several other policy tools. Relending quotas rise by 500bn yuan for agriculture and small businesses and by 200bn yuan for technology upgrades, and China will help cover interest payments on first-time home mortgages.

headline: Vessel is struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 28 September, UK maritime authorities report
detail: The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said it had received a late report of an incident in Hormuz, in which a vessel was hit by a projectile on 28 September.

headline: Iran says it sent a seven-point plan to the US via Qatar and is awaiting an official reply
detail: Iran's foreign minister said Tehran's seven-point plan had been passed to Washington through Qatar and that Iran is waiting for a formal US response.

headline: Iranian army offers a 10bn toman reward for capturing a US soldier as IRGC calls Trump a liar
detail: An Iranian army spokesperson announced the reward for capturing an American soldier, dead or alive. Separately, a Revolutionary Guards spokesperson accused the US president of hiding the truth about Iran's nuclear programme and the effect of Iran's blockade of Gulf energy supplies.

headline: Italy's energy minister is to raise a possible US diesel export ban with the US Energy Secretary on Tuesday
detail: Italy's energy minister said he will speak with US Energy Secretary Wright later on 29 September and will ask about a potential US ban on diesel exports.

headline: Putin bans individuals from taking more than 1m roubles in cash out of Russia to neighbouring countries
detail: The Kremlin published a decree barring cash exports above 1m roubles to EAEU countries, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, with certain exceptions.

headline: EU Court of Justice rejects Poland's bid to suspend provisional application of the EU-Mercosur trade deal
detail: The EU Court of Justice dismissed Poland's application to suspend the EU Council decision authorising provisional application of the EU-Mercosur agreement.

headline: Senior union leader warns the UK PM against ending the pensions triple lock at Labour conference
detail: The Financial Times reported that a senior union leader told the prime minister at the Labour conference that scrapping the state pension triple lock would be electorally reckless.

headline: ECB's Escriva says policy is not yet restrictive and flags concern over rising global long-term rates
detail: ECB Governing Council member Escriva said euro area policy is still not in restrictive territory. He said the upward trend in long-term rates worldwide worries him and could put pressure on interest rates.

headline: US-Iran war adds €100bn to EU fuel bill as energy ministers meet in Dublin, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports the warning that the conflict has added €100bn to the EU's fuel costs. It was issued as the bloc's energy ministers meet in Dublin.

headline: EU energy commissioner rules out an EU-wide windfall tax and says any such levy should be set nationally
detail: The EU energy commissioner said there are no plans for a bloc-wide windfall tax and that any such tax is better set at national level. The commissioner added that, in current market conditions, taxes on electricity should be lower than those on gas.

headline: EU declares full solidarity with Estonia after an attack blamed on Russia
detail: An EU spokesman said the bloc stands in full solidarity with Estonia after an attack that has been blamed on Russia.

headline: US official says Putin envoy Dmitriev held constructive talks with US officials on ending the war in Ukraine
detail: According to a US official, Dmitriev met US officials on Monday to discuss a peaceful settlement of the war in Ukraine and possible US-Russia energy initiatives once the war ends.

headline: IMF projects a $54bn funding gap for Ukraine by 2029, reports say
detail: Reports say the IMF expects Ukraine to face a financing shortfall of $54bn by 2029.

headline: Qatar says it is passing messages and possible solutions between the US and Iran as talks continue
detail: A spokesman for Qatar's foreign ministry said meetings are ongoing and that Qatar is relaying messages between the American and Iranian sides. The spokesman also accused the Netanyahu government of repeatedly trying to undermine Gaza ceasefire efforts.

headline: Union leader warns PM Burnham that ending the pensions triple lock would be electoral insanity
detail: According to the FT, a senior union leader gave the warning before the Prime Minister's first party conference speech as Labour leader. The Resolution Foundation and NIESR have both published calls to replace the triple lock.

headline: ECB's Escriva says high energy prices could become embedded in inflation but sees no second-round effects so far
detail: Bank of Spain Governor and ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said elevated energy prices might anchor in inflation, but that second-round effects are not yet visible. He also said Spain is not considering moving its gold reserves.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev meets US Treasury and Energy Department officials in Washington, reports say
detail: According to sources cited in reports, including Tass, Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev met representatives of the US Treasury and Energy Departments in Washington. The reports say this followed talks with Kushner and Witkoff in New York.

headline: Markets price a 70% chance of a Fed hike on 28 October and 100bp of hikes by end-2027
detail: An economist's note puts market odds of a Federal Reserve rate rise at the 28 October meeting at 70%, with 100bp of tightening priced by the end of 2027.

headline: US house prices rise faster than expected in July, with FHFA up 0.3% on the month and Case-Shiller 20 up 2.47% on the year
detail: The FHFA house price index rose 0.3% month on month in July, against forecasts of 0.1% and 0.0% previously, and was up 2.6% on the year. The Case-Shiller 20-city index rose 2.47% year on year, against forecasts of 2.2% and 2.1% previously.

headline: Saudi oil exports are back near 6 mb/d, their pre-war level, but at much higher prices
detail: An economist's note says Saudi Arabian crude exports have returned to about 6 million barrels a day, roughly where they were before the war, while prices are much higher and Iran remains under blockade.

headline: Lithuania's prime minister says the country is ready to pay for a permanent US troop deployment
detail: Lithuania's prime minister said the country is willing to meet the cost of permanently stationing US forces there.

headline: EU plans no talks to renegotiate Ukraine's export quotas, reports say
detail: According to reports, the EU has no plans to reopen negotiations on export quotas for Ukrainian goods.

headline: PM Burnham pledges to stick to fiscal rules, says VAT comes off electricity bills on Thursday and plans to allow public water ownership
detail: In his conference speech, UK Prime Minister Burnham said the government will keep to the fiscal rules and must be honest about what the country can afford within them. He said VAT will be removed from electricity bills on Thursday, and set out a national energy plan, energy market reform, a Great British grid, an aim to bring energy costs in line with neighbouring countries within 10 years, and legislation to repeal the ban on public ownership of water companies.

headline: GeoPark plans to begin operations at Venezuela's Bare oilfield in December
detail: GeoPark's chief executive said operations at the Bare field will start in December. He added that the company has found about 80 opportunities for horizontal drilling in Venezuela.

headline: South Korea demands an apology from Ukraine for disclosing the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul
detail: South Korea has objected to Kyiv revealing that it transferred North Korean soldiers, who were captured while fighting for Russia, to Seoul, Semafor reports.

headline: PM Burnham pledges to build a national care service
detail: The UK Prime Minister said a dedicated social care service is the only real answer on social care and pledged to create a national care service. No costings or funding details were reported.

headline: GeoPark puts investment at Venezuela's Bare oilfield at $7bn, with output of up to 90,000 bpd by 2038
detail: A GeoPark executive said investment in the Bare oilfield is estimated at $7 billion and that production could reach 90,000 barrels per day by 2038. The company plans to begin operations at the field in December.

headline: China opens a joint military support and training centre in Laos
detail: China's Ministry of National Defence said on Tuesday that it has opened a new military support and training centre in Laos, Reuters reports. Reuters describes it as a rare overseas expansion for China.

headline: PM Burnham says the pensions triple lock will be adjusted from April 2030 to fund a national care service, not through borrowing
detail: The Prime Minister said the triple lock stays in place for his current term and will be adjusted from April 2030. He said the change will produce significant savings to fund a national care service in the next parliament, with no new borrowing, and that low-income pensioners will not pay income tax this parliament.

headline: IRGC says US Navy ships have pulled back to 500km from the Strait of Hormuz
detail: A spokesman for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps made the claim, according to Tasnim News. The US has not been reported confirming it.

headline: Gilt futures give back about 10 ticks as PM Burnham links triple lock savings to social care and calls for welfare rethink
detail: UK gilt futures gave back about 10 ticks of earlier gains after PM Burnham said savings from ending the pensions triple lock would pay for social care. In the same speech he said the welfare system needs a fundamental rethink.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield rises to 5.587%, its highest level since May 2004
detail: A market newswire reported the US 30-year Treasury yield at 5.587% on 29 September, its highest since May 2004.

headline: US Conference Board consumer confidence falls to 81.9 in September, below the 89.0 forecast
detail: The Conference Board's US consumer confidence index came in at 81.9 for September. That compares with a forecast of 89.0 and a previous reading of 89.4.

headline: US JOLTS job openings fall to 7.079m in August, below the 7.228m forecast
detail: US job openings for August came in at 7.079m, compared with a forecast of about 7.228m and 7.271m the previous month.

headline: Irish plant supplying alumina to Russia may be targeted in the EU's next sanctions package
detail: Semafor reports that an Irish factory supplying alumina to Russia could face penalties in the EU's upcoming package of sanctions against Russia.

headline: PM Burnham says a UK-EU summit later this year will set out options for the long-term relationship with the EU
detail: The Prime Minister said the UK needs a higher level of growth, that the current relationship with the EU is not good enough and that Brexit has done more harm than good. He said he will seek consensus on a single option at the summit and will not set out a clear path until the long-term relationship is decided.

headline: Colombia's August oil output falls 2.32% year on year to 732,717 bpd, and commercial gas output falls 10.38%
detail: Colombia's National Hydrocarbon Agency reported average August oil production of 732,717 bpd. Commercial gas production fell to 717 million cubic feet per day.

headline: UN Security Council extends the mandate of Haiti's Gang Suppression Force by six months to 31 March 2027
detail: The UN Security Council adopted a resolution renewing the mandate of the Gang Suppression Force in Haiti for a further six months.

headline: Resolution Foundation says ONS productivity revisions make the OBR's productivity growth assumption look more pessimistic
detail: In a new note, the Resolution Foundation says the ONS's revised productivity estimates raise questions for the OBR's latest productivity growth assumption. It adds that the OBR probably did not receive the data in time to take it into account at the Budget.

headline: IFS calls triple lock change a significant improvement but says it will not cover the cost of universal social care
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies responded on 29 September to the Prime Minister's triple lock announcement at Labour Conference. Its deputy director said better reform options existed and that the change would not be enough to fund universal social care.

headline: EU warns energy prices will be very high as a difficult winter approaches
detail: The European Union has warned of very high energy prices and a challenging winter ahead, according to a market news feed on 29 September. No figures were given.

headline: EU proposes delaying its methane rules to ease pressure on energy supplies
detail: A market newswire reports that the EU has proposed postponing the bloc's methane regulations to relieve pressure on energy. No timetable or figures were given.

headline: Putin says Russia will deepen ties with Republika Srpska and defend its interests, including at the UN Security Council
detail: Russia's President Putin said Moscow will keep developing relations with Republika Srpska across several areas. He pledged to protect its interests, including at the UN Security Council.

headline: European Commission says it plans no talks with Ukraine to renegotiate export quotas under the DCFTA
detail: A European Commission spokesperson said no discussions are planned with Ukraine on renegotiating export quotas under the current trade agreement. The spokesperson added that trade data so far show the revised tariff-rate quota amounts are fair and balanced.

headline: US single-family house prices rise in July, according to the FHFA
detail: The US Federal Housing Finance Agency reports that single-family home prices increased in July, as higher mortgage rates add to affordability pressures. The report does not give a figure for the rise.

headline: Iran's army says it could strike first if it judges an enemy attack to be imminent
detail: Iran's army said it could launch a pre-emptive strike if it concluded that an attack by an enemy was imminent. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: Trump says the Iran war will end very soon and oil prices will fall sharply
detail: The US president said Iran was faring very badly, that it will not obtain a nuclear weapon, and that the conflict and the nuclear issue would be over very soon. He also said oil prices would drop sharply.

headline: Wells Fargo raises its 2027 oil forecasts to $80-$90 for Brent and $75-$85 for WTI
detail: Wells Fargo lifted its 2027 price targets to $75-$85 a barrel for WTI and $80-$90 for Brent, pointing to ongoing supply risks and the need to rebuild depleted inventories. The bank expects prices to come off recent highs but stay elevated through 2027.

headline: PM Burnham announces the state pension triple lock will move to a smoothed version from April 2030
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the triple lock will be adjusted from April 2030 under the 'smoothed' version the Prime Minister announced this afternoon. Commentators note that the savings are intended to help fund a new social care offer and will not improve the overall public finances.

headline: China announces a rate cut and mortgage subsidies to support its slowing economy
detail: Reuters reports that China announced measures on Tuesday to direct cheaper credit to sectors including infrastructure and technology, alongside more support for home buyers.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield rises to 5.595%, its highest level since 2002
detail: A market newswire reports that the US 30-year Treasury yield has reached 5.595%, the highest since 2002.

headline: EU oil coordination group says supply is stable for now but raises concerns over prices
detail: The EU's oil coordination group has found oil supply stable for the time being, according to market newswire reports. The group also noted concerns about prices.

headline: PM Burnham signals broad-based tax rises after 2030 to fund a national care service
detail: An economist commenting on the speech says Burnham said everyone would need to contribute towards a national care service, meaning broad-based tax rises, but not until after 2030. The economist also says savings from the reformed triple lock would not be enough to fund the service.

headline: EU oil coordination group says refineries are running near maximum capacity and sets its next meeting for 15 October
detail: The EU oil coordination group reported that EU refineries are operating close to maximum capacity, and its next meeting is scheduled for 15 October. The European Commission said it would call an additional meeting if needed.

headline: PM Burnham's spokesman does not rule out the UK rejoining the EU
detail: On 29 September, Prime Minister Burnham's spokesman declined to rule out the UK rejoining the European Union.

headline: China says EU members' reported drafting of Section 301-style trade tools would disrupt supply chain stability
detail: China responded to reports that EU member states are drafting trade tools similar to Section 301 and said such measures would disrupt the stability of supply chains.

headline: UK official says the state pension change will save £15bn by 2040
detail: A UK government official put the savings at £15bn by 2040. The change is the move to a smoothed version of the triple lock from April 2030, which PM Burnham announced earlier.

headline: China says it will respond if the EU goes ahead with discriminatory trade measures and calls for dialogue
detail: China said it would take countermeasures if the EU adopts measures it regards as discriminatory, and urged the bloc to settle disputes through dialogue. This follows reports that EU members are drafting Section 301-style trade tools.

headline: Kremlin aide says work has not started on a possible Putin-Trump meeting at the November APEC summit
detail: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said preparations have not yet begun for a possible meeting between President Putin and President Trump at the APEC summit in November.

headline: BoE's Taylor says the case for further rate rises is not compelling unless energy costs stay high and feed wider inflation
detail: MPC member Alan Taylor said policy should not respond mechanically to energy price moves that stay mainly relative-price shocks, and that further tightening would need evidence that second-round effects are taking hold. He described a non-trivial risk to inflation, said the economy has so far proved less prone to a repeat of 2022, and said policy will at some point need to move the other way once energy risks fade, calling for a response that is vigilant but disciplined.

headline: US 52-week bill auction clears at 4.4%, up from 3.98%, with bid-to-cover falling to 3.07
detail: The US Treasury sold $54bn of 52-week bills at a high rate of 4.4%, against 3.980% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover was 3.07, down from 3.61, and 70.21% of bids were allotted at the high.

headline: Russia says it struck a dry cargo ship in the north-western Black Sea
detail: Russia's defence ministry said its forces hit a cargo vessel it said was carrying military supplies for Ukraine's armed forces in the north-western Black Sea, according to Interfax.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield extends rise to 5.612%, highest since June 2002
detail: The US 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.612%, above the 5.595% reported earlier in the session, according to a market post.

headline: EU energy commissioner sees no immediate risk to European energy supplies before winter and reviews transport fuel costs
detail: EU Energy Commissioner Jorgensen said there is no immediate risk to Europe's energy supplies ahead of winter. He added that the EU is looking at ways to make transport fuels more affordable before winter.

headline: US offers up to 40 million barrels of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
detail: The US Energy Department said in a statement that it is releasing up to 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The posts give no further terms or timing.

headline: BoE's Mann says inflation remaining above 2% is a credibility problem
detail: MPC member Catherine Mann said that inflation staying above the 2% target poses a credibility problem for the Bank of England.

headline: Czech PM Babis says Czechia would honour NATO commitments if Russia attacked a Baltic state
detail: Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis told a Czech news website on Tuesday that the Czech Republic would be ready to respond to a Russian attack on a Baltic country, according to Reuters.

headline: ECB's DeMarco does not rule out an October rate hike and says firmer core inflation could justify action
detail: ECB policymaker DeMarco said stronger core inflation could be a reason for the ECB to act and that a rate rise in October should not be excluded. The remarks were reported on 29 September.

headline: Iran links nuclear talks to resolving the Strait of Hormuz issue and a lifting of the US blockade, diplomatic source says
detail: RIA, citing an Iranian diplomatic source, reported that Iran will discuss its nuclear programme only once several conditions are met, including a resolution of the Strait of Hormuz issue and Washington lifting its blockade.

headline: France's debt agency plans €340bn of medium and long-term bond issuance in 2027, net of buybacks
detail: France's debt agency, the AFT, puts next year's state borrowing requirement at €339.7bn, with redemptions at a record €189.2bn, and expects the stock of T-bills to rise by €2.2bn. Its assumptions have 3-month bills at 3% and the 10-year benchmark at 4.3% next year.

headline: ECB's DeMarco says the recent rise in long-term bond yields is quite worrying and the economy is fragile
detail: ECB policymaker DeMarco said the recent rise in long-term bond yields was quite worrying and described the economic situation as quite fragile. The remarks came as US longer-term borrowing costs reached their highest level in almost 25 years, according to the Financial Times.

headline: EU energy commissioner says he has discussed a possible oil release with the IEA chief
detail: EU Energy Commissioner Jorgensen said he had discussed a possible oil stock release with IEA Executive Director Birol. He added that talks with member states and the IEA are still needed.

headline: UK PM Burnham pledges to seek consensus on closer ties with the EU
detail: Reuters reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged on Tuesday to seek a consensus on closer UK ties with the European Union.

headline: BoE MPC member Taylor gives NIESR Dow Lecture on inflation, expectations and the risk of persistence
detail: NIESR says MPC member Alan Taylor is giving this year's Dow Lecture, covering inflation, expectations, the risk of persistence and what they mean for policy. The post did not report any remarks from the speech.

headline: UK government announces triple lock change, moving state pension uprating to a long-run earnings link
detail: The Resolution Foundation's chief executive said the change announced today ties the state pension to earnings over the long run, with each year's rise set at no less than inflation or 2.5%. She said it ends the permanent ratchet of pensions rising faster than earnings.

headline: White House urges EU to release emergency diesel inventories to bring down global prices, sources say
detail: Sources say the White House has asked the European Union to draw down its emergency diesel stocks to lower global prices. This follows the US offer of up to 40 million barrels of oil from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

headline: BoE's Taylor questions whether OIS rates clearly signal market expectations for Bank Rate
detail: MPC member Alan Taylor said he is not convinced that OIS rates give a clear read of what markets expect for Bank Rate, and that he is not a fan of using them that way.

headline: BoE's Taylor sees no clear sign of second-round inflation effects building, in contrast with 2022
detail: MPC member Alan Taylor said he does not see a clear signal of second-round effects building, unlike in 2022. He added that wage growth expectations holding at about 3% would be reassuring.

headline: UK PM Burnham pledges a national care service and an end to the pensions triple lock after the next election
detail: The Financial Times reports that Prime Minister Burnham has promised to create a national care service, end the pensions triple lock and reopen the Brexit debate after the next general election.

headline: Russia's 2027 budget plans raise debt servicing costs by 21.6% and cut welfare, education and health spending
detail: Russian fiscal documents show debt servicing costs rising 21.6% in 2027 to 9.4% of total spending. The same documents show planned cuts to welfare, education and healthcare funding.

headline: Fed's Barr says inflation risks have increased and further policy adjustments are likely to be needed
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr said he sees no clear trend towards a timely return to 2% inflation and that risks to the labour market have receded. He expects US GDP growth to pick up a little in the second half from a 2% pace in the first half, and said it is too early to know whether AI will push up the neutral rate.

headline: Drone fires on a ship on the southern Strait of Hormuz route, Iran's Fars News reports
detail: Fars News, citing local sources, reported that a drone targeted a ship it described as violating rules on the southern route through the Strait of Hormuz. No market reaction was reported in the inputs.

headline: BoE's Taylor flags upside risks to food inflation and links rising oil futures to 2022-type inflation risk
detail: MPC member Alan Taylor said there is considerable upside risk to food inflation. He also said that each rise in oil futures curves increases the risk of a 2022-type inflation scenario.

headline: BoE's Taylor doubts a one-off insurance rate hike could be delivered without being read as the start of a series
detail: MPC member Alan Taylor said he was unsure the Bank could raise Bank Rate once as insurance without markets interpreting it as the first of several hikes.

headline: US says several EU states have released less oil and refined products from reserves than promised
detail: The Trump administration said a number of EU member countries have fallen short of their pledged releases of crude and refined products from emergency stocks.

headline: Iran's Major General Rezai says Tehran has set out its conditions and accuses Trump of being unable to decide
detail: Senior Iranian military figure Mohsen Rezai said Iran has stated its conditions, while saying the US president cannot make decisions, according to IRIB News.

headline: Fed's Barr points to elevated wage rates in skilled trades and says supply and demand must be brought back into balance
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr said some skilled trades are seeing elevated wage rates and that, over the longer term, policy must do what is needed to balance supply and demand. The remarks add to his earlier comments that inflation risks have increased.

headline: US Treasury sanctions 10 individuals and entities over weapons procurement for Iran's defence ministry
detail: The US Treasury says it has sanctioned 10 individuals and entities that obtained weapons and weapons components for Iran's Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL). Reports also say the Treasury has sanctioned Tabatabai, an Iranian official based in Beijing.

headline: US Agriculture Secretary Rollins says more US agricultural products will be shipped to China
detail: US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said on 29 September that more US agricultural goods will go to China. She gave no volumes or timing.

headline: Middle East oil exports climb to their highest since the Iran war began as Hormuz shuttle services resume flows
detail: The Financial Times reports that shuttle services through the Strait of Hormuz have lifted Middle Eastern oil shipments above 80% of the prewar daily average.

headline: BoC's Gravelle says the bank will run operations as needed to hold its policy rate as repo imbalances push CORRA higher
detail: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Gravelle said the bank will tolerate only limited upward pressure on CORRA, and that more active use of two-week repos could at times take reserves above its estimated steady-state demand of C$50bn to C$70bn. He also said the Bank of Canada and OSFI issued a joint statement that using the Standing Liquidity Facility for overnight liquidity is neither exceptional nor a sign of stress.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says business margins are high but beginning to narrow
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said US business profit margins remain high but are starting to thin.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee warns expected future AI productivity gains raise the risk of overheating now
detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said expectations of future productivity gains from AI create a high risk of the economy overheating in the present. His remarks came on 29 September.

headline: White House presses EU to release emergency diesel stocks to bring down global fuel prices, sources say
detail: Reuters, citing two sources, reports that the White House has asked the EU to draw down its emergency diesel inventories. The request is one of several options the Trump administration is pursuing to ease fuel costs before November's midterm elections.

headline: UK PM Burnham's social care plan would scrap the pensions triple lock to fund free care in England
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Prime Minister's plan would end the triple lock on state pensions. The savings would pay for social care in England that is free at the point of use.

headline: Fed's Musalem says the Fed should explain its policy framework but its framework does not promise a set rate path
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said central banks should tell the public how and why they make policy decisions. He said a framework that is understood brings private expectations into line with the Fed's aims, and that stepping back from communication altogether would pose inflation risks.

headline: White House reportedly weighs European diesel reserve release as a way to avoid a US diesel export ban
detail: Politico reports that the White House is looking at a release of Europe's diesel reserves as an alternative to a US export ban. This follows earlier reports that Washington is pressing the EU to release emergency diesel stocks.

headline: UN Security Council extends mandate of international security force in Haiti by six months
detail: The UN Security Council voted on Tuesday to extend the mandate of the international force fighting armed groups in Haiti by six months, Reuters reports. The vote follows fresh killings by gangs.

headline: Fed's Barr says the US economy is strong, inflation has been too high and AI is pushing up costs in the short term
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr made the remarks in an interview with Detroit radio station WJR. He said inflation running too high has left people frustrated and uncertain.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the Federal Reserve Act does not require the Fed to keep bond or stock markets happy
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the Fed's mandate contains no requirement to satisfy the bond market or to avoid surprising equity markets.

headline: BP's Whiting refinery proposes a six-year contract to union as labour talks continue
detail: BP's Whiting refinery said it has offered the USW 7-1 union a six-year contract term with a longer notice period before any strike or lockout. It said talks with union representatives will continue.

headline: UK counter-terrorism police find no explosive devices in probe into suspected plot against airbase used by US forces
detail: Counter-terrorism police said on Tuesday that no improvised explosive devices had been found in their investigation of a suspected plot targeting a British airbase used by US forces for strikes on Iran, Reuters reported.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee calls for a rethink of looking through supply shocks after five and a half years of inflation above target
detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the approach of looking through supply shocks needs revisiting. He described inflation's five and a half years above the Fed's target as playing with fire.

headline: Puntland forces free a petroleum products tanker that Somali pirates seized in April
detail: Security forces in Somalia's semi-autonomous Puntland state rescued the Palau-flagged tanker MT Honour 25, according to Puntland state television on Tuesday, as reported by Reuters.

headline: Brent crude futures drop more than 2% as Middle East oil flows show signs of recovery
detail: Brent crude futures fell by more than 2% late on 29 September, with the move put down to signs that crude flows from the Middle East are recovering.

headline: Bank of Canada's Gravelle says government bond purchases for the balance sheet may not start until 2028
detail: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Gravelle said purchases of Government of Canada bonds are likely to start later than planned and may not begin until 2028.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says oil prices could fall fairly quickly but getting refineries back online is the harder problem
detail: In further remarks on 29 September, Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said oil prices could come down relatively quickly, but the bigger challenge is restoring refinery operations. He also told listeners to watch productivity.

headline: IFS publishes analysis of PM Burnham's triple lock changes, which take effect in 2030–31
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies has published an assessment of the changes to the state pension triple lock announced by Prime Minister Andy Burnham. It says the reform comes into effect in 2030–31.

headline: Fed's Williams sees one further hike as likely this year if the economy performs as expected, but no urgency after September's hike
detail: New York Fed President Williams said policy will respond to data, he projects US inflation at 3.5% this year and back at the 2% target in 2028, and it is imperative that high inflation does not become entrenched. He sees US GDP growth of 2.25% this year and unemployment at 4% over 2027, and said AI investment is an increasingly big issue for inflation.

headline: Fed's Musalem says rates cannot be eased on expected AI productivity gains, with AI capex currently adding to demand pressure
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said the AI capital spending boom is driving demand, and productivity gains and supply relief are not yet visible.

headline: Germany cuts fuel tax from 1 October as Middle East crisis pushes up fuel prices
detail: A CGTN report says the German government is reducing fuel tax from 1 October to ease pressure from rising fuel prices linked to the Middle East crisis.

headline: Fed's Musalem says the case for looking through supply shocks weakens when shocks come one after another
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said repeated supply shocks raise the risk that broader inflation becomes entrenched. In the same remarks he described US growth as strong and the labour market as being in a good place, adding that this depends on growth continuing.

headline: Fed's Musalem says about half of current inflation comes from persistent demand pressure, with long-run expectations anchored at 2%
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said roughly half of inflation now reflects persistent demand pressure. He added that inflation expectations remain consistent with 2% inflation over the long run.

headline: Fed's Musalem suggests anonymously linking rate dots to economic projections to improve the SEP
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said the Fed's Summary of Economic Projections could be improved by connecting each participant's anonymous rate projection to their economic forecasts. The remark was reported on 29 September.

headline: Fed's Musalem says monetary policy is still somewhat accommodative despite the latest rate hike
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem described the US policy stance as still somewhat accommodative after the Federal Reserve's most recent rate increase. These remarks add to his earlier comments today.

headline: Fed's Williams expects inflation to ease as the largest shocks have mostly passed, and says US is less exposed to energy
detail: New York Fed President Williams said inflation should come down because the biggest shocks have largely run their course. He added that energy prices still matter a great deal to the economy, but the US is less exposed to them than in the past.

headline: Mediators step up efforts to end the stalemate between the US and Iran, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that mediators are working to break the deadlock between Washington and Tehran. The report gave no further details.

headline: BP offers six-year labour contract at its 440,000 bpd Whiting refinery as union talks go on
detail: Reuters reports that BP on Tuesday proposed a six-year labour contract for workers at its 440,000-barrel-per-day Whiting refinery in Indiana. Negotiations with United Steelworkers Local 7-1 are continuing.

headline: Traders scale back bets on an October Fed hike and now price one more hike by year-end after Williams remarks
detail: Market pricing moved after New York Fed President Williams said there was no urgency for further action following September's hike. Traders now expect only one more Fed rate hike by the end of the year.

headline: Fed's Williams says AI is pushing up asset valuations and early data show it lifting productivity
detail: New York Fed President Williams said AI is raising asset market valuations, which strengthens the wealth effect. He added that some data are beginning to show AI supporting productivity gains.

headline: US sanctions 10 individuals and entities accused of procuring weapons for Iran's defence ministry
detail: The US Treasury Department said on Tuesday that the 10 individuals and entities it has sanctioned include some based in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan. It said they helped Iran's Ministry of Defence obtain weapons and components.

headline: Oil futures settle lower: Brent down 2.56% at $102.59/bbl, US crude down 3.48% at $89.38/bbl
detail: Brent crude futures settled $2.69 lower at $102.59 a barrel. US crude futures settled $3.22 lower at $89.38 a barrel.

headline: BoE's Taylor doubts a single rate hike is practical without fuelling market bets on further increases
detail: Reuters reported on Tuesday that Bank of England MPC member Alan Taylor said it was unclear whether the Bank could make a single rate hike to curb inflation without prompting unwarranted market speculation of further hikes.

headline: US consumer confidence falls to near 12-1/2-year low in September
detail: Reuters reported that US consumer confidence dropped sharply in September to its lowest in nearly 12-1/2 years. Households expect business and labour market conditions to worsen over the next six months, against a backdrop of the Middle East conflict and rising interest rates.

headline: Euro falls to 16-month low against the dollar at $1.13415
detail: The euro was last down 0.26% at $1.13415, its lowest level against the US dollar in 16 months.

headline: Iran warns regional states of consequences over Netanyahu's visit to the UAE
detail: Fars News reported that Iran's Foreign Ministry warned countries in the region of the consequences of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's visit to the United Arab Emirates.

headline: OPEC+ delegates signal the group is likely to keep its planned steady output quotas
detail: Delegates say OPEC+ is expected to stay with its existing plan of steady production quotas. No figures were given.

headline: Somali pirates kill five crew of hijacked tanker MT Honour 25 before security forces rescue it, Puntland says
detail: Authorities in Puntland say pirates killed five crew members on board the hijacked tanker MT Honour 25. Security forces then rescued the vessel.

headline: Iran's presidency says Tehran will make no concessions on its nuclear rights
detail: Iran's President's Office said the country would not compromise on its nuclear rights and called this a central point of the President's speech, according to state broadcaster IRIB News.

headline: Fed Governor Barr argues further US rate hikes are likely needed to bring inflation down
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said on Tuesday that high energy prices and a jump in AI-related investment have set back progress towards the Fed's 2% inflation target, Reuters reported. He argued again for more rate increases.

headline: UN raises alarm over reports that a Myanmar military air strike near the Bangladesh border killed 50 people
detail: On Tuesday the United Nations expressed alarm at reports that a Myanmar military air strike near the border with Bangladesh killed 50 people and wounded dozens more, according to Reuters. Many of the wounded are reported to be in a critical condition.

headline: Kpler: Middle East oil shipments rise to nearly 80% of prewar levels despite US-Iran tensions
detail: Research firm Kpler found that oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and on routes bypassing it reached nearly 80% of prewar levels last week, Semafor reported.

headline: Fed's Williams says rising bond yields tighten financial conditions at the margin
detail: New York Fed President Williams said higher yields tighten financial conditions at the margin, but he does not see them as a sign of changing longer-run inflation expectations. He also said AI has not so far caused big changes in job levels.

headline: US stocks and bonds fall as inflation concerns keep yields elevated
detail: A US market wrap reported that equities and Treasuries both fell on Tuesday, with inflation concerns keeping yields high.

headline: Russian glide bomb attack on Ukraine's Sumy kills two, officials say
detail: Officials said Russian glide bombs hit homes and a school in the northern Ukrainian city of Sumy on Tuesday, killing two people and injuring six, Reuters reported.

headline: US bank regulators find no deficiencies in resolution plans of 15 banks with more than $250bn in assets
detail: US bank regulators reported on 29 September that their review found no deficiencies in the 'living wills' filed by 15 banks, each with assets above $250bn.

headline: Grynspan reportedly leads fourth UN Security Council straw poll for next UN Secretary-General
detail: Reports say Rebeca Grynspan won the most votes in the fourth straw poll to choose the next UN Secretary-General. The reports gave no vote counts.

headline: European gas storage is reported well below usual levels before winter after curbs on Hormuz tanker traffic
detail: Semafor reports that restrictions on tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz disrupted Europe's usual summer refilling of gas stocks, leaving reserves far lower than normal as the EU looks for extra supply before winter. The report gives no storage figures.

headline: UAE vice president visits Saudi Arabia, the first senior UAE visit since the rift between the two Gulf states last year
detail: Reuters reports that UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and the Saudi defence minister on Tuesday. It is the first visit to the kingdom by a senior UAE official since a deep rift opened between the two countries last year.

headline: API data show US gasoline stocks up 2.991m barrels and distillate stocks down 0.286m barrels
detail: Weekly American Petroleum Institute figures show gasoline inventories rose by 2.991m barrels, after a 2.16m draw the previous week. Distillate stocks fell by 0.286m barrels, compared with a 2.164m draw previously.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield hits its highest level since 2002 as inflation and borrowing concerns weigh
detail: Treasury yields rose on concerns over persistent inflation, government spending and rising corporate borrowing, with the 30-year yield at its highest since 2002. The S&P 500 closed down 0.2%, the Dow down 0.3% and the Nasdaq 100 up 0.2%.

headline: API data show US crude stocks up 1.019m barrels, against a forecast draw of 1.9m
detail: The American Petroleum Institute reported a weekly US crude inventory build of 1.019m barrels, against a forecast 1.9m draw and a previous build of 1.786m. The gasoline and distillate figures were reported earlier.

headline: Trump is set to announce a $54bn Alaska LNG plan, with funding reported to come from a South Korea investment deal
detail: President Trump is due to set out a $54bn liquefied natural gas project in Alaska. People familiar with the plan say the money will come from an investment agreement with South Korea.

headline: API data show crude stocks at the Cushing hub up 0.233m barrels
detail: American Petroleum Institute weekly data show Cushing crude inventories rose by 0.233m barrels, following a 2.082m-barrel rise in the previous week; no forecast was given.

headline: US offers to lend up to 40m barrels of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, its last batch under a global release deal
detail: The US government said on Tuesday it is offering energy companies loans of up to 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. This is the final US tranche of a global agreement to release reserves after the war on Iran.

headline: North Korea rejects Seoul's findings on DMZ mine blast that injured South Korean troops and warns of a catastrophic situation
detail: North Korean state news agency KCNA said South Korea had fabricated its findings on the blast, denied that North Korean troops crossed the military border and warned that the South could face a catastrophic situation. It also said the barriers it is building along the border are an exercise of sovereignty with no military purpose.

headline: Fed's Williams says there is time to assess data before the next hike and expects one more rise before year-end
detail: New York Fed President John Williams said on Tuesday that the Federal Reserve has time to weigh incoming economic data before deciding when to raise rates again. He added that one more increase is likely before the end of the year, Reuters reported.

headline: UK chief executives back pensions triple lock action but prepare for possible tax rises in next month's Budget, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that business leaders welcomed the government's action on the pensions triple lock. They are preparing for possible tax rises in the Budget due next month and say the focus from Burnham and Healey on the cost of business has left them unclear.

headline: Burnham says Labour will pledge to drop the pensions triple lock in a future manifesto; Reform UK and Conservatives attack the plan
detail: On Tuesday the Prime Minister said he would lead Labour on a manifesto pledge to scrap the triple lock, a policy previously backed by all major parties. Reform UK and Conservative leaders criticised the move, City AM reports.

headline: Japan's August industrial output falls 1.7% m/m against forecasts of a rise; retail sales growth slows to 2.7% y/y
detail: Government data show industrial output fell 1.7% on the month, after -0.2% previously, against forecasts of a 1.3% to 1.7% rise; retail sales rose 2.7% year on year against forecasts of 3.2% to 3.3%. Manufacturers expect output to rise 3.2% in September and 3.1% in October.

headline: South Korea's August industrial output falls 2.2% y/y against a forecast 4% rise; retail sales fall 1.8% m/m
detail: The statistics office reports industrial output down 4.8% on the month and 2.2% on the year, against a poll forecast of a 4% annual rise. Service sector output rose 0.5% on the month and retail sales fell 1.8%.

headline: China threatens a firm response if the EU keeps imposing limits on Chinese firms and products
detail: China's commerce ministry called tougher trade measures under consideration by EU states protectionist and unilateral. EU trade chief Sefcovic said he is pushing for G20 and WTO reforms on excess industrial capacity and working with the US and other allies to secure critical mineral supply chains.

headline: US trade representative says tariff caps in trade deals will be considered in setting Section 301 excess capacity tariffs
detail: USTR Greer said caps agreed in trade deals will be taken into account when setting tariffs under the Section 301 probe into excess capacity.

headline: Japan, US and Europe to agree a steel monitoring framework, Yomiuri reports
detail: Japan's Yomiuri newspaper reports that Japan, the US and Europe are set to agree a framework for monitoring steel.

headline: UK car output rises 5.7% y/y in August to 40,872 units, SMMT says
detail: The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders reports UK vehicle production of 40,872 units in August, up 5.7% on a year earlier.

headline: Senior Saudi official denies any meeting between Saudi and Israeli officials
detail: A senior Saudi official denied that any Saudi official had met Israeli officials, according to posts late on 29 September.

headline: Russian missile strike on Kyiv hits homes and energy sites, cutting power to parts of the capital
detail: Witnesses reported explosions in Kyiv from about 00:25 UTC. Later reports described a heavy ballistic missile attack that hit residential areas and energy infrastructure, with outages in parts of the city.

headline: US forces leave their remaining bases in Iraq
detail: Reuters reports that US troops leave their last bases in Iraq on Wednesday. It says the move raises fears of a security vacuum that could help Iranian-backed militias and Islamic State.

headline: South Korea may use surplus tax revenue to cut bond issuance and buy back bonds if yields rise too far
detail: South Korea's finance minister says the ministry is watching the bond market closely and may use excess tax revenue to reduce issuance. He adds that treasury bond buybacks and other steps are possible if yields rise too sharply.

headline: 10-year JGB yield rises 1.0bp to 3.095%
detail: The 10-year Japanese government bond yield is up 1.0bp at 3.095% in Asian trading. WSJ reports short-dated JGBs gaining alongside shorter US Treasurys.

headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at 6.7351 per dollar, weaker than the 6.7025 estimate
detail: The People's Bank of China sets the daily yuan reference rate at 6.7351 to the dollar. Market estimates had been 6.7025.

headline: ANZ survey: New Zealand business confidence falls to 51.9 in September from 53.7
detail: ANZ's September survey shows business confidence at 51.9, down from 53.7. Its own-activity outlook slips to 47.9 from 48.2.

headline: US states act to curb diesel and petrol prices after months of supply disruption
detail: Reuters reports that US states are taking steps to hold down fuel prices, which have risen sharply in recent months. It links the rise to disruption from the US war on Iran, Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and low global inventories.

headline: Israel's finance minister calls for Gaza-style operations in the West Bank and a large arms build-up
detail: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich calls for the approach used in Gaza to be applied in the West Bank, including flattening a neighbourhood in Qalqilya where a tunnel was found. He also calls for an arms build-up larger than the army is seeking and for Israel to expand defence exports.

headline: Lloyds survey: UK business confidence falls to its lowest in 17 months in September
detail: Lloyds' monthly survey shows British firms at their least confident since April 2025. Executives also took a darker view of the global outlook, with the Iran war reported to be raising costs.

headline: Brent rises more than $1 to $103.73 after Trump denies Iran sanctions relief
detail: Brent crude futures gained more than $1 to $103.73 a barrel in Asian trading after President Trump denied that sanctions relief for Iran was planned.

headline: China announces mortgage subsidies for first-time buyers and cuts a policy interest rate
