detail: Beijing is offering support to first-time homebuyers and has cut a policy rate as part of efforts to lift growth, the FT reports. Mainland property stock indices were indicated lower after the announcement, with the Hang Seng Mainland Properties Index seen down 1.3% and the CSI 300 Real Estate Index seen down 5%.

headline: China's official September PMIs: manufacturing 50.1, non-manufacturing 50.2, composite 50.7
detail: NBS manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 from 49.8, in line with forecasts. Non-manufacturing rose to 50.2 from 49.0, above the 49.2 forecast, and the composite rose to 50.7 from 49.5.

headline: Australian August CPI rises to 4.0% y/y from 3.5%, just below the 4.1% forecast; trimmed mean steady at 3.6%
detail: Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m against a 0.5% estimate, while trimmed mean inflation was 3.6% y/y (0.2% m/m) and the weighted median was 3.6% y/y. Building approvals fell 6.1% m/m against a forecast 1.0% fall, and private sector credit rose 0.6% m/m.

headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at its strongest level since 2 February 2023
detail: China's central bank set the yuan's daily reference rate at its strongest level since 2 February 2023.

headline: PBOC injects 833.5bn yuan through overnight reverse repos and conducts no 7-day operations
detail: China's central bank added 833.5bn yuan of liquidity through overnight reverse repos and held no 7-day reverse repo operations, according to its statement.

headline: South Korea's military demands North Korea halt border fortification work and says troops were badly hurt by mines
detail: South Korea's military said North Korea's fortification activity is raising tensions on the peninsula and demanded that it stop immediately and apologise. It also said some of its personnel were seriously injured by North Korean mines.

headline: China's RatingDog September PMIs beat forecasts: manufacturing 52.1, services 51.6, composite 52.4
detail: The private RatingDog survey put manufacturing at 52.1 against a 51.7 forecast and 51.5 in August, and services at 51.6 against 51.3 expected and 51.4 previously. The composite rose to 52.4 from 52.1, and Reuters reported services growth at a three-month high on stronger new orders.

headline: Global bonds head for their worst month in years in September
detail: Reuters reported global bonds weakening on Wednesday, pressured by worsening government finances, heavy issuance and rising inflation. It said energy costs remain high as the US-Israeli war on Iran enters its seventh month.

headline: US forces due to leave their remaining bases in Iraq; Iran's IRGC urges US voters to oust Trump's allies
detail: Reuters reported US troops were due to withdraw from their last bases in Iraq on Wednesday, a departure welcomed by Tehran. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps called on Americans to vote Trump's congressional allies out of office.

headline: South Korean spy agency estimates about 9,000 North Korean soldiers are in Russia
detail: A South Korean lawmaker, citing the spy agency, said there was no sign of further North Korean troop deployments to Russia and that the two countries had cooperated on ballistic missile shipments. The lawmaker also put the chance of North Korea-US talks at the APEC summit at 50%.

headline: China's military runs readiness patrols around Scarborough Shoal
detail: Chinese forces carried out readiness patrols in the sea and airspace around Scarborough Shoal on Wednesday.

headline: Japan's 2-year JGB auction draws a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.89
detail: Japan's Ministry of Finance held a 2-year government bond auction on Wednesday, which drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.89.

headline: China's finance ministry to reopen 80bn yuan of 10-year bonds on 9 October
detail: China's finance ministry said it will sell 80bn yuan of reopened 10-year bonds on 9 October and 20bn yuan of 28-day bills on 8 October.

headline: Poland temporarily shuts Rzeszow and Lublin airports as military aircraft operate; air defences put on readiness
detail: Polish authorities said the two airports were closed temporarily because of military aviation activity. The Polish army said its ground-based air defence and radar reconnaissance systems had reached readiness and that its operational command was monitoring the situation.

headline: Russia says it struck a Kyiv communications centre and energy facilities in the Kyiv region overnight
detail: Interfax, citing Russia's Defence Ministry, reported an overnight strike on a communications centre in Kyiv. The ministry also said energy system facilities in the Kyiv region were hit in what it called a massive strike.

headline: White House holds talks on a possible diesel export ban ahead of the US midterms
detail: The FT reports that the White House is weighing a ban on diesel exports. The report describes a lobbying fight involving President Trump, with oil majors on one side and senior Republicans on the other, who warn of voter anger over high fuel prices.

headline: Vanguard says France's credit is degrading as French borrowing costs rise sharply
detail: The FT reports the warning from Vanguard. It says the Iran war has added to fiscal pressures on Paris ahead of a budget battle.

headline: Dollar is on course for its largest monthly gain against the euro in 14 months
detail: Reuters reports that the dollar is near this year's high against the euro. It cites US growth and rising US interest rates, set against energy and debt concerns in Europe.

headline: Oil prices stay elevated even as Persian Gulf exports recover
detail: The WSJ reports that oil prices remain high despite a recovery in exports from the Persian Gulf. The report gave no price figures.

headline: China imposes an extra 55% tariff on Brazilian beef imports from 1 October
detail: China's commerce ministry said the additional 55% tariff will be charged on top of the rate that currently applies.

headline: Experts put the cost of a fully funded social care model for England at £18.7bn
detail: The FT reports experts saying the prime minister's planned national care service would still leave some elderly people selling their homes to pay for care. They said a model covering all costs would cost £18.7bn and would probably need tax rises.

headline: Kazakhstan restarts enforcement proceedings to recover a 2.3tn tenge fine from the NCOC oil consortium
detail: Kazakhstan has restarted enforcement proceedings to recover a 2.3 trillion tenge fine from North Caspian Operating Company (NCOC), according to an Interfax report.

headline: Gold edges lower as bets on a Fed rate hike and Middle East tensions support the US dollar
detail: Gold prices slipped in early trading on 30 September, with the move attributed to bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike and Middle East tensions supporting the US dollar. No figures were given in the report.

headline: UK GDP grows 0.5% q/q and 1.4% y/y, above forecasts of 0.4% and 1.2%
detail: UK GDP grew 0.5% quarter on quarter against a forecast of 0.4% and a previous reading of 0.4%, and 1.4% year on year against a forecast and previous reading of 1.2%. Business investment rose 1.75% q/q, against a forecast of 1.7% and a previous reading of 1.7%.

headline: UK current account deficit narrows to 19.932bn, smaller than the 25.5bn forecast
detail: The UK current account showed a deficit of 19.932bn, against a forecast of 25.5bn and 22.134bn previously.

headline: Iran's foreign minister takes US feedback on seven-day proposal to Tehran after Doha talks with Qatari mediators
detail: Foreign Minister Araghchi met Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday night and received the US response to the seven-day proposal, which he is due to discuss in Tehran on Wednesday, according to an official briefed on the talks. The official said the main disagreement between the US and Iran concerns sequencing rather than the plan's elements.

headline: German import prices rise 8.3% y/y and 1% m/m, both above forecasts
detail: German import prices rose 8.3% year on year, against a forecast of 8% and 6.8% previously. On the month they rose 1%, against a forecast of 0.7% and 0.2% previously.

headline: German real retail sales rise 1.3% m/m, below the 1.5% forecast, after a 3.4% fall
detail: German real retail sales rose 1.3% month on month, against a forecast of 1.5%. The previous reading was a 3.4% fall.

headline: PM Burnham says the UK should consider options for its EU relationship, including eventually rejoining
detail: Reuters reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that Britain should weigh options for its future relationship with the European Union, including rejoining the bloc in the longer run. He is stepping up efforts to rebuild ties with Europe.

headline: UK Q2 business investment rises 5.2% y/y against a 0.8% forecast; exports up 2.8% q/q, government spending down 0.5%
detail: The Q2 GDP breakdown shows business investment up 1.8% q/q, gross fixed capital formation up 0.9% q/q against a 1.2% forecast, and private consumption up 0.3% q/q, in line with forecasts. Exports grew 2.8% q/q and imports were flat; both had been forecast at 0.5%. Government spending fell 0.5% q/q against a forecast of -0.3%.

headline: PM Burnham says cutting the welfare bill will allow the UK to meet its defence goals
detail: The Prime Minister linked lower welfare spending to paying for the UK's defence spending commitments. No figures were given.

headline: Oil rises after Trump denies he is willing to ease sanctions on Iran
detail: Reuters reports oil prices rose on Wednesday after US President Trump denied he would ease sanctions on Iran, while Qatar pushed for peace talks. Prices had fallen in the previous session as Middle East crude supply recovered.

headline: PM Burnham plans to change the pensions triple lock from 2030 to fund a national care service and admits a possible funding shortfall
detail: City AM reports that the Prime Minister announced the triple lock will be adjusted from 2030, in effect becoming a double lock, with the savings going to a new national care service. He acknowledged the plans may face a shortfall, and economists cited in the report said taxes would need to rise.

headline: Ministers tell business groups the uncapped overnight stay levy will let mayors take on more borrowing
detail: City AM reports that at Labour's Business Day, ministers told leading business groups that the new uncapped tourist tax would allow mayors to increase their borrowing.

headline: UK real household disposable income per head rises 1% in Q2 to £6,577
detail: ONS figures reported by City AM show real household disposable income per head rose 1% in the second quarter to £6,577. The increase was driven by higher benefit payments, which grew faster than wages.

headline: Senior source says seven-day plan needs significant changes before progress can be discussed
detail: Al Arabiya cites a senior source as saying the seven-day proposal needs significant changes before any progress can be discussed. This follows the Iranian foreign minister taking US feedback on the plan back to Tehran after talks in Doha.

headline: Israeli PM and security minister hold urgent talks with senior security officials, sources say
detail: Alaraby TV, citing sources, reports that the Israeli Prime Minister and security minister are holding urgent talks with senior security officials. No further details were given.

headline: French flash HICP falls 0.4% m/m against -0.5% forecast; consumer spending drops 0.5% and PPI rises to 4.8% y/y
detail: Preliminary French HICP fell 0.4% m/m against a forecast of -0.5%, after a 0.7% rise the month before. Consumer spending fell 0.5% m/m against a flat forecast, after a 0.5% rise, and producer prices rose 4.8% y/y, up from 3.4%.

headline: Drone attacks in Russia's Bryansk region kill one person and injure another, says regional governor
detail: The governor of Russia's Bryansk region said drone attacks had killed one person and injured another. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK energy price cap forecast to rise to nearly £2,000 from January as the Iran war lifts prices
detail: The Financial Times reports a forecast that the household energy price cap will rise to nearly £2,000 for January to March. That would be the biggest increase in four years, driven by higher prices linked to the Iran war.

headline: French September flash HICP rises to 3.4% y/y against a 3.2% forecast; CPI rises to 3.0% y/y
detail: France's preliminary September HICP rose to 3.4% y/y, above the 3.2% forecast and up from 2.6%. National CPI rose to 3.0% y/y against a 2.8% forecast, up from 2.4%.

headline: Russia extends its ban on diesel exports to the end of October
detail: Interfax reported on 30 September that Russia has extended its diesel export ban through October. The report gave no market reaction.

headline: PM Burnham says rejoining the EU is an option as the government reviews UK relations with the bloc
detail: The Financial Times reports that the prime minister said full EU membership is an option under consideration. The comments come as the government carries out a review of Britain's relationship with the 27-member bloc.

headline: Iraq's oil exports average 2.65m bpd in September, including 250,000 bpd via Turkey's Ceyhan port
detail: A spokesperson for Iraq's oil ministry gave the September average for daily oil exports as 2.65 million barrels per day. Of that, 250,000 bpd went through the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

headline: US formally ends Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq
detail: The US has formally brought its Operation Inherent Resolve military mission in Iraq to an end. The input does not report any market reaction.

headline: Riksbank Governor Thedeen says the Swedish economy is stronger than expected
detail: Sweden's central bank governor, Erik Thedeen, said on Wednesday 30 September that the Swedish economy has been unexpectedly strong. No figures or policy guidance were given in the report.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield rises above 5.61%, its highest level since 2002
detail: Bloomberg reported that the US 30-year yield went above 5.61% on Tuesday, with inflation concerns and growing bets on Fed rate rises adding to the bond sell-off.

headline: Iran gets US response on seven-day trust-building plan through Qatari mediators in Doha
detail: Reuters reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi received the US feedback in Doha on Tuesday. An official briefed on the talks said the order of steps was the main sticking point.

headline: France is the worst-hit G7 government bond market in the sell-off linked to the Iran war
detail: The FT reported that French bonds have fallen more than any other G7 market as fiscal pressure and political risk build ahead of an election. Vanguard said further losses were possible.

headline: Resolution Foundation backs proposed changes to the state pension triple lock, citing lower long-run fiscal cost
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the proposed changes to the triple lock take significant uncertainty and long-run cost out of the public finances while keeping pensioner incomes rising. The post does not give details of the proposals.

headline: German unemployment rises by 12,000 in September against a forecast rise of 500; jobless rate holds at 6.4%
detail: German seasonally adjusted unemployment rose by 12,000 in September, against a forecast of 0.5k and a previous rise of 4k, taking the total to 3.012m from 2.996m. The unemployment rate stayed at 6.4%, in line with forecasts; the unadjusted total was 2.994m against 3.061m previously.

headline: Bavaria September CPI rises to 3.2% y/y from 2.9%; up 0.6% m/m
detail: Bavarian consumer prices rose 3.2% year on year in September, up from 2.9% the previous month, and 0.6% month on month, up from 0.2%. The regional figure comes ahead of Germany's national flash inflation reading.

headline: Swiss ZEW expectations fall to 2.6 from 12.1
detail: The Swiss ZEW expectations index fell to 2.6 in the latest reading, down from 12.1 previously.

headline: Polish airports in Lublin and Rzeszow reopen after closures for military aviation operations
detail: Poland's Air Traffic Authority said on Wednesday that flights had resumed at Lublin and Rzeszow airports after temporary closures due to military aviation operations, Reuters reported.

headline: North Rhine-Westphalia September CPI rises to 3.3% y/y from 2.9%
detail: The annual inflation rate in Germany's most populous state rose to 3.3% in September from 2.9% the previous month. No forecast was given.

headline: Germany orders state-owned energy company SEFE to store gas
detail: The German government has told SEFE to put gas supply into storage, according to a market newswire report. No volumes or timing were given.

headline: Italian consumer confidence falls to 91.2, missing 94.4 forecast; manufacturing confidence rises to 91.9
detail: Italy's consumer confidence index fell to 91.2 in September from 94.5, against a forecast of 94.4. Manufacturing business confidence rose to 91.9 from a revised 90.2, beating the forecast of 90.5.

headline: Flydubai flight bound for Israel is diverted to Saudi Arabia
detail: A Flydubai flight heading to Israel was diverted to Saudi Arabia, Reuters reported. No reason for the diversion was given.

headline: UAE energy minister backs OPEC+ and says demand for additional oil output is rising
detail: UAE Energy Minister Mazrouei said the country supports the OPEC+ group and will keep coordinating with partners and consumers. He also said demand for extra oil production is increasing.

headline: Germany to set up a strategic gas reserve from 2027
detail: A German Economy Ministry spokesperson said the government will set up a strategic natural gas reserve from 2027. The spokesperson also said the economy minister told state-owned SEFE to raise gas storage because of ongoing geopolitical risks.

headline: Iran's foreign minister tells cabinet Tehran has received a US proposal, government spokesperson says
detail: A spokesperson for the Iranian government said in a post on X that Foreign Minister Araqchi had told the cabinet about a proposal received from the United States. The post gave no details of what the proposal contains, and the batch reports no market reaction.

headline: BBC reports UK energy bills set to rise 16% in January, below the 24% rise the BoE assumed a couple of weeks ago
detail: A Resolution Foundation economist cited the BBC report and put the smaller rise down to a slight fall in wholesale gas prices. The Resolution Foundation separately said energy prices will also rise next month.

headline: Egypt says eight Egyptian crew members from tanker MT Honour 25, hijacked off Somalia, have been released
detail: Egypt's foreign ministry announced the release of the eight crew members who had been on the hijacked tanker in Somalia.

headline: PM Burnham says he is open to rejoining the EU after the next election, with customs union and single market options also possible
detail: City AM reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday morning that all options for the UK's future relationship with the EU are on the table. He said these include a customs union, the single market or full EU membership.

headline: Australian private credit firm Metrics Credit Partners freezes redemptions from some funds and delays its financial reports
detail: Reuters reports that Metrics Credit Partners, one of Australia's largest private credit firms, has frozen investor redemptions from some funds and delayed the release of its financial reports. Reuters describes this as the latest sign of stress among non-bank lenders.

headline: Italian September flash CPI rises to 4.2% y/y and HICP to 4.1%, both above 3.7% forecasts
detail: Italy's preliminary September CPI is up 4.2% y/y (previous 3.3%) and 0.7% m/m (forecast 0.3%). HICP is up 4.1% y/y (previous 3.2%) and 2.0% m/m (forecast 1.7%).

headline: OPEC+ expected to hold November output targets steady at Sunday meeting, sources tell Reuters
detail: Two sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters that OPEC+ producers are likely to leave production targets for November unchanged when they meet on Sunday.

headline: Israeli official calls incident on diverted Israel-bound Flydubai flight a terrorist attack, i24 reports
detail: An Israeli official told broadcaster i24 that the incident on the Flydubai flight bound for Israel, which was diverted to Saudi Arabia, was a terrorist attack. No further details were given.

headline: Trump may unveil plan as soon as Wednesday to use about $54bn of South Korean investment for Alaska LNG project
detail: Reuters reports that President Trump could set out plans as soon as Wednesday to fund an Alaska liquefied natural gas project from about $54bn of South Korea's pledged strategic investment package. The project faces doubts, according to Reuters.

headline: PM pledges to amend the state pension triple lock next parliament
detail: The Resolution Foundation reported the Prime Minister's commitment to change the triple lock in the next parliament and said the move would help the public finances. No details of the changes were given in the post.

headline: Burnham says a major review of European policy will consider the UK rejoining the EU
detail: According to the Financial Times, Andy Burnham said the review will look at the option of rejoining the EU, after saying in his Labour conference speech that Brexit had done more harm than good.

headline: Witness reports a loud explosion in central Kyiv
detail: A witness reported hearing a loud explosion in central Kyiv on 30 September. No further details on the cause or damage were given, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: Russia extends its diesel export ban for fuel producers to the end of October
detail: Reports on Wednesday said the Russian government has kept its ban on diesel exports by fuel producers in place until the end of October.

headline: US formally ends Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq, reports say
detail: Reports say the United States has officially concluded Operation Inherent Resolve, its military mission in Iraq.

headline: BoE FPC says risks are now more likely to crystallise at the same time than in July; gilt repo reforms due early 2027
detail: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee said higher oil and gas prices have made the supply shock more protracted and that risky credit, including parts of private credit, remains vulnerable to tighter financing, while markets have so far withstood higher energy prices and bond yields. It said it will set out bank leverage ratio and gilt repo reform proposals in early 2027, that the repo reforms will offset risks from the leverage changes, and that households, companies and banks remain resilient.

headline: German 10-year Bund auction yields 3.58%, up from 3.39%, with cover falling to 1.2 from 1.5
detail: Germany's 10-year Bund auction produced an average yield of 3.58%, against 3.39% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.2, down from 1.5.

headline: UKMTO receives a late report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency has received a report, made some time after the event, of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. No further details were given.

headline: Suspected plot against UK airbase used by US forces for Iran strikes was foiled after a suspect called police, Times reports
detail: The Times reported on Wednesday that one of the men later arrested at the British airbase had alerted police, which led to the suspected plot being thwarted. Reuters carried the report.

headline: Japan's PM pledges to strengthen supply capacity as prices and rates rise, and to review revenue and spending
detail: Japan's prime minister says the government will boost supply capacity amid rising prices and interest rates. The PM also says it will assess trends in tax receipts and review revenue and spending.

headline: Kremlin dismisses reports of sanctions relief in return for freeing political prisoners, saying Russia holds none
detail: The Kremlin calls reports of a possible easing of sanctions in exchange for prisoner releases irrelevant and says Russia has no political prisoners. It also says Putin will address the newly elected parliament later on Wednesday.

headline: Kremlin confirms contacts with US on possible prisoner exchange and responds to its nuclear warnings to NATO over Kaliningrad
detail: At the same briefing where it rejected reports of sanctions relief for prisoners, the Kremlin confirmed it is in contact with the United States about a possible prisoner exchange. On Russia's nuclear warnings to NATO over Kaliningrad, it said its diplomats are reminding European leaders of the region's founding documents.

headline: Japan's economy minister says government and BoJ share the same view on the economy and prices
detail: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi said there was no difference in understanding between the government and the Bank of Japan on the economy and prices.

headline: Satellite imagery shows China has built a new military support centre in Laos, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that satellite imagery shows China built the facility on farmland in Laos over the past year, extending its overseas military presence into Southeast Asia.

headline: BoE Governor Bailey urges governments to step up testing of frontier AI models before public release
detail: In the first of a series of letters on artificial intelligence, the Bank of England governor warned that advanced AI poses sophisticated threats to banking, markets and payments systems, City AM reports.

headline: German September flash HICP rises to 3.3% y/y from 2.9%, above 3.2% forecast; CPI also 3.3% against 3.1% expected
detail: Preliminary German figures put September HICP at 3.3% y/y and 0.6% m/m, against forecasts of 3.2% and 0.5% (previous 2.9% and 0.2%). CPI rose to 3.3% y/y from 2.9%, above the 3.1% forecast.

headline: US ADP private payrolls rise by 90,000 in September, above forecasts
detail: The ADP employment change for September came in at 90,000. The posts give different figures for the forecast and the previous reading, but both put the result above consensus.

headline: US August PCE inflation slows to 3.4% y/y against 3.7% forecast; core PCE eases to 3.0% against 3.3% expected
detail: US data show headline PCE prices at 3.4% y/y, down from 3.7%, and core PCE rising 0.2% m/m against a 0.3% forecast, taking the annual rate to 3.0% from 3.3%. Personal income rose 0.2% m/m against a 0.5% forecast, spending rose 0.9% as expected, and spot gold was reported up 0.6% at $4,206.29/oz after the release.

headline: US Q2 GDP revised up to 2.2% in final estimate, above 1.5% forecast; Q2 core PCE revised down to 3.3%
detail: The final US estimate puts second-quarter GDP growth at 2.2%, up from 1.5% and above the 1.5% consensus, while Q2 core PCE prices were revised down to 3.3% from 3.6% and headline Q2 PCE to 5.0% from 5.3%. The US advance goods trade deficit for August widened to $132.6bn against a $115bn forecast.

headline: EU says it is open to discussing whatever relationship options the UK proposes
detail: The EU said it is willing to engage on options the UK may put forward for their relationship. This follows PM Burnham's review of UK relations with the bloc, which he said could include rejoining.

headline: French 10-year yield spread over Germany widens 5bp to 124bp
detail: The gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields widened by 5bp to 124bp on Wednesday afternoon.

headline: Fed finalises stress test changes, saying they will not materially change aggregate bank capital requirements
detail: The Federal Reserve says its changes should cut the year-on-year volatility of bank capital requirements by roughly 50%. Governor Barr voted against the final rule, saying it will weaken the stress test.

headline: Analysts estimate Gulf crude exports are back to near pre-war levels
detail: Goldman Sachs puts crude exports from Persian Gulf producers at 19m b/d and says the recovery came from higher exports through Hormuz. JPMorgan estimates the exports are at 98% of pre-war levels.

headline: US September Chicago PMI jumps to 58.8 from 47.1, well above 51.0 forecast
detail: The MNI Chicago business barometer for September came in at 58.8, against a consensus of 51.0 and a previous reading of 47.1.

headline: US diesel futures rise 4.5% and gasoline futures 2.9% after weekly EIA storage data
detail: US diesel futures added to earlier gains after the Energy Information Administration's weekly storage report. They were up 4.5%, while gasoline futures held a 2.9% rise.

headline: ECB's Schnabel says strong credit growth suggests financial conditions are not yet restrictive
detail: In a speech, ECB Executive Board member Schnabel said high costs reach consumers faster when the economy is resilient, and that robust credit dynamics suggest financial conditions are not yet restrictive. She added that the economy might respond more than assumed to the recent rise in global yields, which would dampen price pressures, and that inflation can be brought back to target more gradually if expectations stay anchored.

headline: ECB's Lagarde calls France's 120%-of-GDP debt serious and says it needs a credible budget path
detail: In an interview with the newspaper La Croix, ECB President Lagarde said France's debt is serious at 120% of GDP and has no path to coming down, and that the country needs a credible budget trajectory and reforms to restore confidence. She also said the European financial system is more solid now than it was in the 2008 and 2011 crises.

headline: PM Burnham says fuel duty is under review ahead of the Budget and rules out unfunded plans
detail: The Prime Minister said everything is being looked at before the Budget, including fuel duty, and that the Budget cannot contain unfunded plans. He also said the government will do what it can despite difficult public finances.

headline: PM Burnham says there are strong indications Iran was involved in the RAF Fairford incident
detail: The Prime Minister said the UK is working closely with the US administration after five suspects were released on bail, the FT reports. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Italy plans to spend €14bn under the EU escape clause to cut energy costs for firms, PM Meloni says
detail: Italian PM Meloni announced that the spending will be funded through the EU fiscal escape clause. She also said the EU's proposed revision of the ETS carbon trading scheme is inadequate.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs to 5.29%, a fresh high since 2007
detail: A market commentator reported the US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.29%, its highest level since 2007. It comes after the 30-year yield rose above 5.61%, its highest since 2002, earlier in the session.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.304%, its highest level since May 2002
detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.304%, rising from the 5.29% level reported earlier in the session and reaching its highest since May 2002.

headline: Trump says Fed Chair Powell should be forced to resign and asks the Attorney General to review a Fed report
detail: US President Trump said Federal Reserve Chair Powell should be forced out and asked Attorney General Blanche to review a Fed report. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: UK and EU agree to hold November summit, pushing talks on industrial subsidies into next year
detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK and Brussels will go ahead with a key summit in November. The two sides have agreed to defer negotiations on industrial subsidies until next year.

headline: BoJ Tankan: large manufacturers index rises to 24, short of 25 forecast; large non-manufacturers falls to 35
detail: The Bank of Japan's September Tankan put the large manufacturers index at 24, up from 22 but below the 25 forecast. The large non-manufacturers index fell to 35 from 37 against a 36 forecast, and firms expect consumer prices to rise 2.6% over a year, down from 2.7% previously.

headline: Fed's Kashkari says inflation must return to 2% after a long overshoot and warns supply shocks could lift expectations
detail: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said the Fed must bring inflation back to 2% given the extended period above target, and that rolling supply shocks risk raising inflation expectations. He also described the rise in bond yields as a global trend.

headline: France plans record bond issuance next year with debt at about 119% of GDP
detail: France said it will sell a record amount of government bonds next year, according to Semafor, which reported that the French spread over German bonds widened after the announcement.

headline: BoJ September summary of opinions shows several members favour further rate rises, with one saying hikes should speed up if inflation…
detail: In the Bank of Japan's summary of its September meeting, one member said the terminal rate could end up above estimates and market expectations, and another said the Bank should not be overly cautious given upside risks to inflation. A Cabinet Office representative said the government expects the BoJ to weigh the cumulative impact of past rate increases.

headline: US Secretary of State Rubio orders Iran's UN delegation out of the US as negotiations reach deadlock, Axios reports
detail: Axios reports that Rubio called for the Iranian delegation to leave the US after the UN General Assembly ended, with US-Iran negotiations at a deadlock, according to a US official.

headline: RBA Financial Stability Review says high asset prices and leverage leave global markets open to a sharp correction
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia says the main threats to domestic financial stability come from overseas, and that more leveraged investors in bonds and equities add to volatility. It says private credit is not currently a risk to overall stability and that about 2% of owner-occupier borrowers face cash-flow shortfalls.

headline: JGB yields rise across the curve: 10-year up 5bp to 3.110%, 30-year up 6bp to 4.200%
detail: In Asian trading, Japan's 10-year government bond yield rose 5.0bp to 3.110% and the 20-year rose 4.5bp to 3.945%. The 30-year yield gained 6.0bp to 4.200%, and dollar/yen rose 0.5% to 158.19.

headline: UK Nationwide house prices fall 0.2% m/m in September; annual growth slows to 0.8% from 1.6%
detail: Nationwide reports September house prices fell 0.2% on the month, against a forecast of 0.0% and a 0.2% rise previously. The annual rate eased to 0.8% from 1.6%.

headline: Swiss September CPI rises to 1.0% y/y from 0.8%, matching forecast
detail: Swiss annual consumer price inflation was 1.0% in September, in line with the 1.0% forecast and up from 0.8% the previous month.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises further to 5.33%, its highest level since 2002
detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.33%, above the 5.304% reported earlier, according to a market wire post.

headline: Japan PM Takaichi pledges to control total annual JGB issuance across initial and supplementary budgets
detail: Japan's Prime Minister said the government will manage total annual government bond issuance, counting both the initial and the supplementary budgets. Earlier in the session, 10-year and 30-year JGB yields had risen to 3.110% and 4.200%.

headline: Chinese refiners suspend October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice, sources say
detail: Reuters, citing four people briefed on the matter, reports that Chinese refiners have stopped exporting oil products to destinations other than Hong Kong and Macau until Beijing says otherwise. One refiner has cancelled cargoes.

headline: US Treasuries end their worst quarter since 1994 as yields hit two-decade highs for a seventh straight session
detail: Reuters reports that US yields reached two-decade highs for a seventh consecutive session on Thursday. A fall in oil prices later steadied bond markets.

headline: US reportedly presses France and Germany to release emergency diesel stocks, raising the prospect of a US diesel export ban
detail: Three sources say the US has told France and Germany to release emergency diesel reserves or face a possible US ban on diesel exports. One source says the US wants the EU to release 120 million barrels of diesel over the next six months.

headline: Eurozone September final manufacturing PMI is revised up to 52.9 from the 52.7 flash reading
detail: The final eurozone manufacturing PMI for September came in at 52.9. Both the forecast and the previous reading were 52.7.

headline: French PM targets €43bn in new budget savings, BFM TV reports
detail: French broadcaster BFM TV reports that the prime minister is seeking €43bn of fresh savings in the budget. The report comes as France plans record bond issuance next year, with debt at about 119% of GDP.

headline: French 5-year CDS climb to 71.6bp, the highest since July 2013, as French bonds sell off
detail: France's 5-year credit default swaps reached 71.6bp, their highest level since July 2013. The move came as French government bonds sold off.

headline: UK 30-year gilt yield rises above 6%
detail: A market commentator reported shortly after 08:15 UK time that the 30-year gilt yield had moved above 6%. The FTSE 100 was reported down 2% at about the same time.

headline: Italian 10-year yield rises 10bp to 4.7232%, its highest since November 2023
detail: Italy's 10-year government bond yield reached 4.7232%, up 10bp on the day and its highest level since November 2023, according to a market wire.

headline: UK September final manufacturing PMI comes in at 51.9, below the 52.0 forecast and down from 52.0
detail: The final UK manufacturing PMI for September was 51.9. The forecast was 52.0 and the previous reading was 52.0.

headline: French 10-year OAT auction yields 4.93%, up from 4.23%, with bid-to-cover dropping to 2.0 from 2.28
detail: At the same French government bond sale, the 20-year OAT priced at 5.4%, up from 4.74% at the previous auction, and its bid-to-cover fell to 2.43 from 3.07.

headline: UK announces new sanctions on vessels suspected of carrying Russian LNG
detail: The UK government's latest Russia sanctions package targets shadow fleet ships believed to be transporting Russian liquefied natural gas. The same package also covers Russian military and intelligence officers accused of abusing civilians in Ukraine.

headline: French finance minister presents 2027 budget with €43bn of new measures, €54bn in total, and keeps 3% deficit goal for 2029
detail: French Finance Minister Lescure said the 2027 budget has €43bn of new measures, or €54bn including measures already in place, and that cutting the deficit to 3% of GDP by 2029 is still possible. Budget Minister Amiel said action on the budget cannot wait until next year's election.

headline: ECB's Nagel says the bank's tools are aimed at price stability, not at particular bond yield levels
detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel made the remarks when asked about the rise in bond yields. They come during a sell-off in euro area government bonds.

headline: Trump tells Time that high rates hurt the economy more than inflation and some inflation helps pay down debt
detail: In an interview with Time, US President Trump also said the US will soon be refilling its strategic oil reserves. The interview comes with the US 10-year Treasury yield at its highest level since 2002.

headline: French budget watchdog HCFP calls 2027 growth forecast optimistic but finds 2026 deficit target plausible
detail: France's High Council of Public Finances (HCFP) says the 2026 deficit target is plausible but carries risks. It describes the 2027 budget targets as a significant adjustment and says the deficit goal is a minimum given the country's alarming public finances.

headline: BoE's Mann says a risk-management approach to policy is appropriate given inflation risks
detail: MPC member Catherine Mann said a risk-management strategy is suitable in light of the risks to inflation. No market reaction was reported in the inputs.

headline: BoE's Mann calls for a Bank Rate rise, saying the current policy stance is not tight enough
detail: MPC member Catherine Mann said raising rates can help ensure a lasting return to 2% inflation, and that real and nominal conditions need to stay tight. She also said policy cannot rely on risk premia to do the work of monetary policy and called for a clearly communicated reaction function.

headline: US initial jobless claims come in at 197,000 in week to 26 September, below the 200,000 forecast
detail: US initial claims slipped by 1,000 from a prior week revised up to 198,000. Continuing claims for the week to 19 September were 1.701m, against a forecast of 1.725m.

headline: Fed's Collins says growth is at or above trend and inflation is too high, and gives no steer on the next meeting
detail: Boston Fed President Collins said the US labour market is close to full employment and inflation remains too high. She declined to commit to a policy view ahead of the next FOMC meeting.

headline: Healey calls UK bank chiefs to a pre-Budget summit next week, Sky reports
detail: Sky News reports that Healey has summoned the heads of UK banks to a meeting next week, ahead of the Budget. The report gave no details of the agenda.

headline: US September final S&P Global manufacturing PMI drops to 55.9, short of the 57.0 forecast and down from 57.0
detail: S&P Global's final US manufacturing PMI for September came in at 55.9, compared with a forecast of 57.0 and 57.0 the previous month.

headline: US September ISM manufacturing PMI edges down to 54.5, short of 55.0 forecast, as prices paid rises to 77.9
detail: The ISM manufacturing index came in at 54.5 for September, compared with 54.6 in August and a forecast of 55.0. New orders rose to 55.3 from 53.7, against a forecast of 54.7, and prices paid climbed to 77.9 from 71.1, against a forecast of 73.

headline: US Treasuries fall, led by the 30-year, after the ISM manufacturing prices index jumps
detail: US Treasuries are reported lower, with the long end leading, after the September ISM manufacturing report showed a rise in prices paid. The same report put the employment index at 52.7, above the 52.0 forecast and up from 51.2.

headline: IMF says global bond markets are functioning in an orderly way
detail: The IMF said global bond markets are operating in an orderly manner, at a time when US, French, Italian and UK yields have been rising.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield falls 6bp to 4.827%, briefly touching its lowest level in a week
detail: The US 2-year Treasury yield was reported down 6.03bp at 4.827% after briefly reaching a one-week low.

headline: Money markets scale back ECB rate-rise bets and no longer fully price another hike by year-end
detail: Traders reduced their bets on ECB tightening on 1 October. Money markets no longer fully price three more rate rises, or one more rise by the end of the year.

headline: Money markets stop fully pricing four BoE rate rises by the end of 2027
detail: Traders have scaled back BoE tightening bets and no longer fully price four Bank Rate rises by the end of 2027.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield extends its fall to 10bp on the day, at 4.785%
detail: The US 2-year Treasury yield is down 10bp on the day at 4.785%, extending an earlier 6bp fall.

headline: German government raises 2026 growth forecast to 1.3% from 0.5%, according to draft
detail: A person familiar with the German government's draft forecast says it raises 2026 growth to 1.3% from the 0.5% expected in April. The same draft puts growth for 2028 at 0.6%.

headline: Saudi East-West crude pipeline flows recover to 5.5m barrels a day, Argus reports
detail: Pricing agency Argus reports that throughput on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline has recovered to 5.5m barrels a day. No price reaction was reported.

headline: Italy-Germany 2-year bond yield spread posts its biggest widening since 2020
detail: A market news feed reported that the gap between Italian and German 2-year yields widened by the most since 2020. No figure was given. Euro-area bonds were already under pressure on the day, with the Italian 10-year yield at its highest since November 2023.

headline: Putin rejects proposals for a mutual halt to strikes in the Black Sea
detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin turned down proposals for a mutual end to strikes in the Black Sea, calling them absurd, Russian reports say. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Euro extends its fall against the dollar, down 1% at $1.12165
detail: The euro was last trading 1% lower against the US dollar at $1.12165 on Thursday evening, extending earlier losses.

headline: Fed's Jefferson says the Fed may take more time over its next rate move, hinting at an October hold
detail: Fed policymaker Jefferson said future rate changes should depend on the data and inflation is still above target with upside risks. He also said the September rate rise will help anchor inflation expectations, and he expects unemployment to hold steady to the end of the year.

headline: UK bank shares fall sharply as 30-year gilt yield reaches its highest level since 1998
detail: Reuters reports UK bank stocks dropped sharply on Thursday as 30-year gilt yields hit their highest since 1998. It cites growing concern over UK public finances and exposure to high oil prices and inflation ahead of this month's Budget.

headline: Trump tells aides he expects to resume bombing Iran as US sends third carrier and up to 10,000 more troops to Middle East, WSJ says
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that President Trump has recently told aides he expects to resume strikes on Iran. It also says the US is sending a third aircraft carrier and up to 10,000 more troops to the region. No market reaction is reported in the inputs.

headline: Brent crude extends gains to 4.6% after China suspends oil exports
detail: Brent was last reported 4.6% higher and WTI up 2.8%. The move follows reports that China has suspended oil exports.

headline: WTI crude November futures settle 2.71% higher at $92.87 a barrel
detail: NYMEX WTI November futures settled up $2.45, or 2.71%, at $92.87 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.6420 a gallon and gasoline at $3.4026 a gallon.

headline: Iran offers to let nuclear inspectors in if sanctions are eased
detail: Iran has offered to allow nuclear inspectors access on condition that sanctions are eased, according to a market news report. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Brent crude futures settle 4.37% higher at $102.31 a barrel
detail: Brent crude futures settled up $4.28, or 4.37%, at $102.31 a barrel on 1 October. Earlier in the session the gain had reached 4.6% after China suspended oil exports.

headline: Fed's Cook says supply shocks are having persistent effects and inflation expectations must stay anchored
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Cook said supply shocks have had surprisingly lasting effects and are becoming more important for policy, and that the best policy response could vary by sector. She also said the Fed needs to keep inflation expectations anchored and pay attention to consumer confidence.

headline: Fed's Bowman sees no pressing need for further rate changes this year
detail: Federal Reserve policymaker Michelle Bowman said she sees no urgent need for more rate moves before the end of the year. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield falls 5bp to 5.24%, retreating from its highest level since 2002
detail: A US market wrap reports the 10-year Treasury yield down 5bp at 5.24% by the close, with the S&P 500 up 0.2% as the bond market rallied. Earlier in the session the yield reached 5.33%.

headline: Fed's Kashkari expects further rate rises into 2027 but is undecided on a move this month
detail: Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said on Thursday he expects more rate increases will be needed to restrain the economy going into 2027. He said he is unsure whether the next move should come later this month, Reuters reports.

headline: Markets price out an October Fed rate rise after two senior officials argue for waiting on more data
detail: Reuters reports that remarks this week from two of the Federal Reserve's top policymakers led markets to drop expectations of a rate increase at the Fed's late-October meeting. Both officials said they wanted more data before deciding on the next policy move.

headline: Fed's Logan says the policy rate must rise by at least another 50bp, as current policy is not restrictive
detail: Dallas Fed President Logan said several more rate rises would at minimum be needed to reverse last autumn's cuts and bring inflation back to the 2% target. She added that higher long-term yields may partly reflect larger term premiums, and that the Fed will monitor them.

headline: Tokyo September CPI rises to 2.7% y/y, above forecasts, as core inflation reaches its fastest rate since November 2025
detail: Japanese government data show headline Tokyo CPI at 2.7%, against a 2.5% forecast and 1.9% previously. Core CPI also rose to 2.7% from 1.8%, and the measure excluding fresh food and energy was 3.0%; the national August jobless rate came in at 2.5%, against a forecast of 2.4%.

headline: Japan's economy minister says extraordinary monetary stimulus is no longer needed as Japan is out of deflation
detail: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi said overly loose monetary policy is no longer required and that the Takaichi government aims for both growth and fiscal discipline. He said monetary policy is for the BoJ and he hopes it keeps in close contact with the government.

headline: Dollar holds at 17-month high, heading for a third weekly gain, as the global bond sell-off weighs on the euro
detail: Reuters reports the dollar at a 17-month high, with borrowing costs around the world at multi-decade peaks on inflation concerns linked to higher oil prices. The euro has weakened below $1.1250 ahead of US payrolls data.

headline: DMO announces ad hoc tender of up to £1.5bn of a 2028 gilt on 7 October
detail: The UK Debt Management Office says it will hold an ad hoc tender of up to £1.5bn of a 2028 gilt on 7 October.

headline: ECB's Rehn says higher energy prices are bringing inflation closer to the ECB's adverse scenario
detail: ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn said rising energy prices were moving the inflation outlook nearer to the central bank's adverse scenario. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK 2-year gilt yield drops 9bp to 4.726%, its lowest level since 22 September
detail: The 2-year gilt yield fell 9bp to 4.726% in early trading on 2 October, its lowest since 22 September, according to a market wire post.

headline: BoE Decision Maker Panel: firms see year-ahead CPI at 3.3% in September, with expected wage growth steady at 3.4%
detail: The Bank of England's Decision Maker Panel survey puts firms' year-ahead CPI inflation expectations at 3.3% for September. Firms' expected wage growth for the year ahead held at 3.4% in the three months to September.

headline: FAO says world food prices rose in September to their highest level in nearly four years
detail: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization says its world food price measure climbed in September to a near four-year high. It points to logistics disruptions and weather concerns in crop markets as the causes.

headline: Eurozone September flash CPI rises to 3.8% y/y, above 3.7% forecast and up from 3.2%; core holds in line at 2.5%
detail: The eurozone flash estimate puts September headline inflation at 3.8% year on year, against a 3.7% forecast and 3.2% previously, and at 0.6% month on month, against a 0.5% forecast. Core inflation rose to 2.5% from 2.4%, matching the forecast.

headline: French 5-year sovereign CDS widen further to 81bp
detail: S&P Global Market Intelligence data show French 5-year credit default swaps at 81bp, up from the 71.6bp reported earlier, which was already the highest since July 2013.

headline: France's bond risk premium widens to 150bp, a level last seen in 2012
detail: A market commentator reports that France's sovereign bond risk premium has reached 150bp for the first time since 2012. French bonds are selling off this week after the 2027 budget was presented.

headline: UK average diesel price passes £2 a litre for the first time, RAC says
detail: The RAC reports the average UK diesel pump price has gone above £2 per litre, a level not reached before.

headline: Diesel prices drop sharply as EU weighs releasing 50mn barrels of reserves under US pressure, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports the EU is considering releasing 50mn barrels of diesel reserves after the US president threatened to ban US diesel exports if Europe does not release stocks. Diesel prices were reported to have fallen sharply; no release has been agreed.

headline: NIESR says about two-thirds of the third-quarter rise in 10-year gilt yields came from higher rate expectations
detail: NIESR's latest Term Premium Tracker puts the UK 10-year gilt yield at 5.43% at the end of the quarter, its highest since 2007. It estimates that about two-thirds of the increase came from higher expected interest rates, with the rest from term premium.

headline: French 10-year government bond yield reaches 4.989%, its highest level since 2002
detail: LSEG data show the French 10-year yield at 4.989%, the highest since 2002, as the French bond sell-off continues.

headline: French 2-year government bond yield rises 13.8bp to 3.8337% as the French bond sell-off extends
detail: France's 2-year government bond yield was last up 13.8bp on the day at 3.8337%. The move follows earlier rises in French 10-year yields and a widening in French CDS.

headline: US September nonfarm payrolls rise 29,000, well short of the 84,000 consensus
detail: The US Labor Department reports September nonfarm payrolls up 29,000, against a consensus forecast of 84,000. Average weekly hours are 34.4, compared with a 34.3 forecast and unchanged from the previous month.

headline: US September unemployment rate rises to 4.2% against 4.1% forecast; annual wage growth slows to 3.0%
detail: The US September jobs report shows unemployment at 4.2%, average hourly earnings up 3.0% y/y and a two-month net payroll revision of minus 60,000. US short-term rate futures jumped after the release as traders cut bets on an October Fed rate rise.

headline: Fed-dated swaps stop fully pricing one more US rate rise this year
detail: Fed-dated swaps no longer price a full Federal Reserve rate rise by the end of the year, according to a market post. This comes after earlier moves that priced out an October rise.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says the US Navy has reopened the Strait of Hormuz and crude is flowing through
detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said the US Navy has reopened the Strait of Hormuz and crude oil is passing through again. He added that more energy announcements will follow next week. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says the administration does not aim to inflate its way out of debt and puts higher yields down to a strong…
detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said US interest payments are too high, the President is committed to cutting the deficit and the jobs report was in line with expectations. He said yields are higher because the economy is strong.

headline: Macron says the G7 has decided to release up to 100mn barrels of diesel and crude stocks over four months
detail: French President Macron said G7 countries have agreed to release strategic diesel and crude stocks of up to 100mn barrels. He said the release will take place over four months.

headline: French-German 10-year bond yield spread narrows to 140bp from 159bp
detail: A market newswire reports that the gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields has fallen to 140bp from 159bp.

headline: IEA head Birol says oil prices fell at least $5 after the agency announced a release of oil and diesel reserves
detail: IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said the stocks will go to market over the coming days and weeks, with distribution to be finalised after consultation with member states. He said reserves are sufficient and more can be released if needed.

headline: Italy plans to ask the EU for 2027 deficit leeway of 0.6% of GDP and raises its 2026 growth forecast to 0.8%
detail: Italy's government plans to ask the EU for deficit flexibility worth 0.6% of GDP in 2027, and expects the 2026 deficit to come in below 3% of GDP. It also raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.8%, up from the 0.6% it forecast in April.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee keeps both a rate rise and a pause open, saying the inflation side of the Fed's mandate matters more
detail: Speaking to Fox Business, Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the labour market is steady and he wants to see whether there is evidence that inflation is heading back to 2%. He added that he would not react strongly to a single month of data.

headline: US Justice Department will not reopen its criminal investigation into Fed Chair Powell, Attorney General says
detail: Attorney General Blanche said the Department of Justice is satisfied with the Fed inspector general's report and will not resume the criminal probe into Powell.

headline: Trump rules out a US ban on diesel exports
detail: US President Trump said on Friday that the administration will not impose a ban on diesel exports.

headline: Hedge funds hold a net short position in sterling for the first time since 2024, CFTC data show
detail: Weekly CFTC positioning data released on Friday show hedge funds have moved to a net short position in the pound for the first time since 2024.

headline: Healey expected to use the Budget for targeted support rather than large tax rises, putting off hard choices, FT reports
detail: According to the Financial Times, Chancellor Healey is expected to centre her Budget statement on targeted help for households and businesses. The paper says she is not expected to raise taxes on the scale of recent Budgets.

headline: Bundesbank's Nagel says German growth this year could reach about 1%, around twice recent projections
detail: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said on Friday that strong export demand and government investment could lift German growth to around 1% this year, roughly double the latest projections, Reuters reports.
